brief_summary:
This is a prospective, multicentre, observational registry study with primary data collection designed to evaluate the real-world effectiveness and safety of selumetinib in adult patients with NF1 who have symptomatic, inoperable PN. A total of approximately 800 participants who initiate selumetinib treatment will be enrolled across about 45 investigational sites in China. Sites will be selected based on their diagnostic and treatment expertise in NF1-PN, research capability and sufficient patient pool. Patients who are eligible and willing to participate will be enrolled into the study.

The study includes an approximately 25-month enrolment period and a 96-week observation period. Patients will be followed up until the end of the 96-weeks observation period after first dose of selumetinib, or patient death, lost to follow-up, withdrawal of consent, whichever occurs first. Patients will be followed within 96 weeks period (starting after first dose received) in the study even if selumetinib is discontinued. The study will end until the last participant has the opportunity to complete 96 weeks' assessment.
primary_outcomes: ORR of PN by REiNS criteria.
QoL change from baseline by INF1-QoL(IMPACT OF NEUROFIBROMATOSIS 1 ON QUALITY-OF-LIFE) questionnaire.
title: Observational Study of the Real-world Effectiveness and Safety of Selumetinib Treating Adult Patients With Neurofibromatosis Type 1 (NF1) Who Have Symptomatic, Inoperable Plexiform Neurofibroma (PN)

brief_summary:
The aim of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the effects of placing the Boyle-Davis mouth gag 3 minutes versus 10 minutes after endotracheal intubation on the hemodynamic response in pediatric patients aged 3-12 years undergoing elective tonsillectomy and/or adenotonsillectomy.

The Boyle-Davis mouth gag is routinely used in pediatric tonsil surgery to provide adequate surgical exposure. Mechanical stimulation of the oropharyngeal tissues during mouth gag placement may cause transient changes in heart rate and arterial blood pressure.

At least 40 patients will be enrolled and randomized in a 1:1 ratio into two groups. In one group, the mouth gag will be placed 3 minutes after endotracheal intubation, whereas in the other group it will be placed 10 minutes after intubation. Anesthetic management will be standardized between the groups.

Heart rate and arterial blood pressure will be recorded before induction, immediately before mouth gag placement, and at 1 and 3 minutes after placement. The maximum heart rate observed during the first 3 minutes after mouth gag placement will also be recorded. The primary outcome will be the percentage change in maximum post-gag heart rate relative to the pre-gag heart rate.
primary_outcomes: Percentage Change in Heart Rate After Boyle-Davis Mouth Gag Placement (ΔHR%)
title: Boyle-Davis Mouth Gag Timing in Pediatric Tonsil Surgery

The study plans to enroll 3800 participants randomized 1:1 into one of two treatment arms (Arm A - investigational: atirmociclib plus giredestrant taken continuously in a 28-day cycle) or (Arm B - comparator: placebo plus giredestrant taken continuously in a 28-day cycle). brief_summary:
This two-stage quasi-experimental study will evaluate the effects of empathy-based midwifery education on midwifery students' empathy and anxiety, and on women's satisfaction with childbirth and perceptions of traumatic birth.

In the first stage, third-year midwifery students in the intervention group will receive four face-to-face training sessions over two weeks, totaling 390 minutes. The program will include theoretical instruction, case discussions, role-play, virtual reality activities, mannequin-based simulation, and guided reflection. Students in the control group will continue their usual coursework and clinical practice. Students' empathy and anxiety will be assessed before and after the training.

In the second stage, trained students will provide empathetic communication and psychosocial support to women during labor under the supervision of a faculty member and/or the responsible midwife. Support will include active listening, clear information, reassurance, respect for privacy, and assistance with coping during labor. Women in the control group will receive routine maternity care. Maternal satisfaction with childbirth and perceptions of traumatic birth will be assessed after birth, once the mother and newborn are clinically stable.

The study will examine whether this educational program improves students' empathy, reduces their anxiety, and contributes to more positive childbirth experiences for women.
primary_outcomes: Change in Midwifery Students' Empathic Tendency Scores
title: Psychosocial Effects of Empathy-Based Midwifery Education on Midwifery Students and Pregnant Women

brief_summary: Type I interferonopathies (T1I) are rare autoinflammatory diseases characterized by dysregulated type I interferon signaling, leading to severe multisystem inflammation, including skin and lung involvement. STING-associated vasculopathy with onset in infancy (SAVI) is an autosomal dominant T1I associated with severe systemic inflammation, skin ulcers, and progressive interstitial lung disease. Current treatments are often insufficient, highlighting the need for novel therapeutic strategies. This project aims to develop patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) models, combined with somatic cell differentiation and 3D organoid technologies, to investigate SAVI pathogenesis and assess the feasibility and efficacy of gene editing (GE). By enabling precise correction of disease-causing mutations, GE may overcome the limitations of conventional gene replacement approaches and provide a proof of concept for future targeted therapies.
primary_outcomes: To generate a model of type I interferonopathy to gain insight in STING1 role in nonhematopoietic cells and to explore gene editing as a therapeutic option
title: Combining Gene Editing and iPS to Study and Treat Monogenic Autoinflammatory Diseases

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if adding a medical payment case management service to the hospital's usual follow-up care can reduce the financial hardship of cancer treatment in patients of any age, including children and teenagers, who have a primary bone tumor and are scheduled to have surgery at Shanghai Sixth People's Hospital. It will also learn whether the service lowers the number of families who spend a large share of their yearly income on medical care. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the service improve patients' scores on a questionnaire that measures financial hardship (the COST-FACIT) from the start of the study to 6 months later? Does the service lower the number of families whose out-of-pocket medical costs reach 10% or more of the family's yearly income?

The study will enroll 124 patients, randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to two groups of 62:

Payment service group: patients receive the hospital's usual follow-up care, plus help from a dedicated payment specialist (called a Co-Pay Navigator).

Control group: patients receive the hospital's usual follow-up care only. They can still ask the hospital about payment questions at any time.

Researchers will compare the two groups to see if the payment service reduces financial hardship.

Both groups receive the whole-course patient management program of the hospital's Comprehensive Oncology Center (COC), which includes:

Reminders to return for scheduled check-ups, with alerts if a check-up is missed A record of their medications, with reminders to take them as prescribed Questionnaires they fill in through the program, which the system checks for warning signs that a case manager then follows up Patient education materials about the disease and about follow-up care Online access to a case manager for questions at any time

All participants will also:

Answer short questionnaires about their family's medical costs at the start of the study and again about 3, 6, 9, and 12 months later, on a mobile phone and with help from the study staff if needed Have a parent or other family member who helps care for them answer a short questionnaire about the strain of caregiving

Participants in the payment service group will also work with a Co-Pay Navigator, who:

Reviews the family's insurance coverage and out-of-pocket costs Explains which payment programs the family may be able to use: basic medical insurance, critical illness insurance, supplemental medical insurance, charity programs, drug company assistance programs, social assistance, and fundraising Helps the family apply for these programs and follows the applications Reviews the hospital bill when the patient leaves the hospital Checks in every three months to update the family's payment plan

Taking part does not involve extra clinic visits, blood tests, or study drugs, and the study does not change any medical treatment.
title: Medical Payment Case Management for Financial Toxicity in Patients With Primary Bone Tumors: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
Well differentiated neuroendocrine tumors (NETs) are rare and heterogeneous malignancies that frequently evolve toward advanced or metastatic disease, requiring long-term systemic treatment strategies delivered over multiple lines. Their management is complex and influenced by tumor-related factors-including primary site and grade-as well as disease burden, functional status, patient comorbidities, and access to available therapeutic options. As a result, real-world treatment pathways in advanced NETs are highly diverse.

In recent years, the systemic treatment landscape of advanced NETs has expanded beyond somatostatin analogues (SSA), peptide receptor radionuclide therapy (PRRT), and chemotherapy to include targeted therapies. Among these, multitarget tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) targeting tumor angiogenesis have progressively been incorporated into clinical practice. Their use varies according to tumor subtype, disease dynamics, prior treatments, and patient-related considerations, reflecting the absence of standardized sequencing algorithms.

In routine clinical practice, the choice and sequencing of TKIs are driven by individualized clinical decision-making rather than predefined treatment pathways. Their positioning within systemic treatment strategies is influenced by anticipated benefit, tolerability, prior toxicities, and practical constraints such as regulatory indications, access, and reimbursement conditions, which differ by tumor origin. Consequently, the real-world positioning of TKIs within treatment sequences remains insufficiently characterized at a national level.

"SEQUENCE-NET" is an ambispective observational study designed to prospectively document how TKIs are integrated into systemic treatment strategies for advanced pancreatic and extra-pancreatic NETs in routine clinical practice within the ENDOCAN-RENATEN network.
title: Real World Positioning of Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitors (TKIs) Within Systemic Treatment Strategies for Advanced Neuroendocrine Tumors (NETs)

brief_summary: People with psychotic disorders are at a higher risk of premature death than the general population. Adverse lifestyle factors contribute to this reduced life expectancy; such factors may include high consumption of tobacco and other substances, physical inactivity, and obesity. These lifestyle factors increase the risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and cancer-conditions known as non-communicable diseases (NCDs). Primary care offers an evidence-based and cost-effective method known as "Targeted Health Dialogues" (Riktade hälsosamtal), aimed at individuals in their forties to motivate lifestyle changes. Previous studies indicate that people with psychotic disorders-particularly those with lower levels of social functioning, comorbidities, or concerns about stigma-frequently miss appointments at primary care centers, whereas in outpatient psychiatric care, they may establish long-term therapeutic relationships with specialist nurses. There is thus a need to evaluate the feasibility of using this evidence-based, nurse-led method-Targeted Health Dialogues-to support healthy lifestyle changes and reduce NCD risk among people with psychotic disorders receiving outpatient psychiatric care. The findings of this study will provide a basis for designing nurse-led lifestyle support interventions for individuals with psychotic disorders.
primary_outcomes: Changes from baseline in Body Mass Index after 12 months
title: Targeted Health Dialogues for Individuals With Psychosis Spectrum Disorders

brief_summary:
Background and Rationale Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a genetic disorder caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene, resulting in progressive muscle weakness and multiple complications, including respiratory and cardiac impairment, osteoporosis (OP), and fragility fractures (FF). Bone fragility is a major concern, as lower-limb fractures may accelerate the loss of independent ambulation and complicate daily care. Despite increased life expectancy, bone health in adults with DMD remains insufficiently investigated. This study aims to address this knowledge gap and improve the understanding and management of skeletal complications in this population.

Objectives

The study aims to: (1) determine the prevalence of fragility fractures in adults with DMD; (2) identify childhood and adolescent risk or protective factors affecting adult bone health; (3) collect data on fracture treatment; (4) measure serum analytes involved in bone metabolism and bone-muscle crosstalk; and (5) identify genetic modifiers associated with increased fracture risk.

Study Population

Approximately 200 patients with DMD aged over 18 years will be recruited from 15 Italian tertiary referral centers specializing in neuromuscular diseases. A control group of healthy males aged over 18 years will be recruited exclusively at the coordinating center. Controls will undergo only a blood collection of approximately 3 mL for serum analysis.

Study Design and Procedures Patients will undergo respiratory assessment, including peak expiratory flow (PEF), forced vital capacity (FVC), and respiratory support requirements; orthopedic assessment of scoliosis, contractures, deformities, and previous spinal fusion surgery; motor function assessment using the North Star Ambulatory Assessment (NSAA); upper-limb function assessment using the Performance of the Upper Limb (PUL) scale; and the Six-Minute Walk Test (6MWT). Imaging procedures will include a lateral thoracolumbar spine radiograph (T4-L4) and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) of the lumbar spine (L1-L4) and total body less head (TBLH). Clinical and medical history data will be recorded using a dedicated case report form (CRF).

Biological Samples and Analyses One blood sample of approximately 3 mL will be collected for serum extraction and analysis of metabolites involved in bone metabolism and bone-muscle crosstalk. Samples will be centralized at the coordinating center and then sent to the University of Campania "Luigi Vanvitelli" for analysis. Healthy control samples will be used for comparison.

Two additional blood tubes, totaling approximately 6 mL, will be collected for DNA extraction and genome-wide association studies (GWAS), aimed at identifying genetic modifiers associated with increased fracture risk. These samples will be centralized and subsequently sent to the University of Padua for genetic analysis.

Data Management and Ethics Study data will be anonymized and managed in accordance with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR, EU 2016/679) and the Declaration of Helsinki. Patients and/or their legally authorized representatives will receive the study information and provide written informed consent before participation. Investigators will declare any potential conflicts of interest.

Expected Outcomes The study will characterize bone health and fragility fracture prevalence in adults with DMD, describe fracture management, and investigate clinical, developmental, biochemical, and genetic factors associated with fracture risk. The findings may help improve fracture prevention, bone health monitoring, and clinical management in this population.
primary_outcomes: Prevalence of Fragility Fractures in Adult Patients with DMD
title: Bone Health in Adults With Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy: A Survey on Osteoporosis, Fractures and Treatment.

brief_summary: Patients with drug-resistant epilepsy may have cardiac dysautonomia, with reduced heart rate variability and increased sympathetic tone. This condition is part of the concept of "epileptic heart" and could be a risk factor for sudden death, one of the main causes of excess mortality in patients with severe epilepsy in adulthood. The mechanism of this cardiac impairment is poorly understood. The hypothalamus, due to its role as the subcortical conductor of the autonomic nervous system and its known links with the limbic system, particularly the amygdala and hippocampus, is a candidate for a key intermediary role in the impact of seizures on cardiorespiratory function. The investigators wish to investigate the hypothesis that cardiac dysautonomia in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy is correlated with structural changes in the hypothalamus. The investigators wish to study in 7Tesla MRI the volume of the different hypothalamic nuclei, the amygdalo- hypothalamic and hypothalamo-bulbar connectivity, as well as the metabolic content in spectroscopy in patients with drug-resistant epilepsy, and correlate these data with the sympathetic and parasympathetic tones of these patients.
primary_outcomes: Correlation coefficient between the volume of the posterior hypothalamic nucleus with the degree of cardiac autonomic function impairment
title: Study of the Link Between Structural Alterations in the Hypothalamus and Cardiac Dysautonomia in Drug-resistant Epilepsy
