brief_summary:
Bone marrow edema (BME) is a radiological finding characterized by increased fluid content and structural changes within the bone marrow. It most commonly affects weight-bearing joints such as the hip, knee, and ankle. Patients with BME may present with pain during activity or at rest, tenderness, swelling, joint effusion, and limitation of joint motion. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is considered the gold standard for diagnosis.

BME is commonly observed in patients with knee osteoarthritis (OA) and may be associated with increased pain, impaired joint function, and progression of structural joint damage. Therefore, recognition and treatment of BME may be clinically important in patients with knee OA.

Treatment options for BME include conservative and surgical approaches. Standard conservative treatment generally includes activity and weight-bearing modification, analgesics and nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, and physical therapy modalities. Extracorporeal shock wave therapy (ESWT) is one of the non-invasive physical therapy options that can be added to standard conservative treatment. Surgical treatment, including core decompression, may be considered in patients who do not respond to conservative treatment.

ESWT may exert beneficial effects by improving local blood flow, promoting angiogenesis, stimulating bone remodeling and regeneration, and providing analgesia. Previous studies in patients with knee-related BME have suggested that ESWT may reduce pain, improve functional outcomes, and decrease BME findings on MRI. Kang et al. reported more rapid improvements in pain, functional outcomes, and the MRI-detected area of BME within three months with ESWT compared with alendronate therapy. Sansone et al. found that ESWT resulted in greater reductions in pain and BME area, together with clinically meaningful improvement at three months, compared with conservative treatment consisting of unloading and analgesics. In a prospective randomized controlled trial, Gao et al. further showed that ESWT provided more favorable six-month outcomes in terms of pain, functional scores, and MRI-assessed BME area than intravenous prostacyclin combined with oral bisphosphonate therapy. Collectively, these findings suggest that ESWT may provide sustained clinical and radiological benefits in patients with knee BME.

This study aims to investigate the effects of adding ESWT to standard conservative treatment in patients with knee osteoarthritis accompanied by bone marrow edema. Patients receiving active ESWT will be compared with those receiving sham ESWT in terms of pain, functional outcomes, patient satisfaction, and changes in bone marrow edema volume on MRI.
conditions: Bone Marrow Edema of the Knee
interventions: Sham Radial Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy
primary_outcomes: Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) Findings: Volumetric Assessment of Bone Marrow Edema
title: Extracorporeal Shock Wave Therapy in the Treatment of Periarticular Bone Marrow Edema in Patients With Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary:
This study will test whether adding a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) device, which shows personal glucose patterns, improves dietary self-management over the first 6 weeks. Both groups receive the same digital health program, standardized education, and support for setting behavioral goals. It will include 860 residents of Namwon, Republic of Korea, aged 40 years or older who have elevated fasting glucose or documented type 2 diabetes diagnosis or treatment.

After screening, participants will be assigned by chance to one of two groups of 430. Assignment is preferably on the first screening visit but may occur later. The actual assignment date is Day 0. The device group will use one CGM sensor for approximately 10 days after assignment. The wait-list control group will receive the same education and behavioral goal-setting support during the first 6 weeks, without a CGM device. Researchers will compare dietary self-management scores at week 6, before the control group receives a sensor.

After the week 6 assessment and data lock, the control group will also be offered a sensor so that all eligible randomized participants have an opportunity to use the device. This later offer is not the main intervention comparison. Week 12 assessments provide exploratory follow-up after both groups have been offered a device. Researchers will also assess application use, body weight, waist circumference, blood pressure, and safety. The research team will not change medicines based on sensor readings, and usual medical care will continue.
interventions: Continuous Glucose Monitoring With Application-Based Biofeedback
Common Standardized Education and Behavioral Goal Setting
Common Digital Health Program and Basic Health Counseling
title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring and Dietary Self-Management in Adults in Namwon

brief_summary:
This study aims to explore how information from different types of biological tests, such as genetic, protein, and fat-related analyses, can help doctors better identify and distinguish patients with systemic autoinflammatory diseases (SAIDs), including undifferentiated or complex forms of these conditions (uSAIDs and SAIDs), as well as fibromyalgia. The goal is to improve diagnosis and help identify the most appropriate treatments and care options for each patient.

The study will also develop computer-based tools to identify important biological patterns in patients' medical records and laboratory results. These tools will help doctors interpret each patient's individual case and better understand their condition.

Finally, the study will bring together biological test results, clinical information, and the findings from these analyses in a single, comprehensive health record. This record will have an easy-to-use interface designed to support patients' care teams. Its usefulness in everyday clinical practice will then be evaluated.
primary_outcomes: Assessment of the usability and usefulness of the SHE system
title: Development of a Cloud Platform for Advanced Diagnostics Based on Clinical and Omics Data.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if subthreshold micropulse laser is a safe, effective, and painless treatment for multifocal and recurrent central serous chorioretinopathy (CSCR) in adults.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does subthreshold micropulse laser reduce the fluid under the retina, as measured by optical coherence tomography (OCT)?
* Does it improve vision and lower the chance of the disease coming back?

Participants will:

* Have a full eye examination, including vision testing, OCT, and fluorescein angiography before treatment.
* Receive subthreshold micropulse laser treatment, which is painless and does not damage the retina.
* Return for follow-up visits at 1, 3, and 6 months for vision testing and OCT scans.
* Receive a repeat laser session at 3 months if fluid is still present.
title: Treatment of Recurrent and Multifocal Central Serous Chorioretinopathy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to find out whether using a real-time continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) system can improve daily blood sugar control compared with usual self-monitoring of blood glucose (SMBG; finger-stick testing) in people with diabetes who are treated with insulin.

This study will include adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who have less-than-ideal blood sugar control while using insulin. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does CGM-guided diabetes management lead to a larger decrease in HbA1c from baseline to about 6 months than SMBG-guided management?
* Does CGM use increase the time that glucose stays in the target range and reduce low blood sugar episodes, without causing new safety problems?

Researchers will compare two groups. One group will use the RIGHTEST iFree 2 CGM system together with a smartphone app to view glucose data in real time. The other group will use standard finger-stick blood glucose monitoring with an approved blood glucose meter as their main tool for checking glucose. Both groups will continue to receive routine diabetes care from their usual health-care providers.

Participants will take part in regular clinic visits over approximately 6 months. At these visits, study staff will review glucose records, adjust diabetes treatment if needed, and collect information such as HbA1c and other blood tests, device data, and questionnaires about quality of life and diabetes-related distress. Safety information and any device problems will also be recorded. The results will help determine whether CGM can be used as a routine tool to improve long-term blood sugar control in people with diabetes.
primary_outcomes: Change in glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) from baseline to Week 24
title: Randomized Trial of the RIGHTEST iFree 2 CGM System for Glycemic Control in Adults With Diabetes Mellitus

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of a resistance exercise program on serum Insulin-like Growth Factor 1 (IGF-1) levels in patients with knee osteoarthritis. Specifically, it aims to investigate the relationship between changes in serum IGF-1 levels and clinical improvement after exercise therapy, and to evaluate the impact of the presence of osteoarthritis metabolic phenotype on this relationship.

Participants will be asked to complete a structured resistance exercise program for 8 weeks.

Researchers will compare the pre-exercise and post-exercise serum IGF-1 levels, clinical scores (WOMAC, VAS) and radiological findings (MOAKS Osteophyte Score) to determine the effectiveness of the intervention.
lead_sponsor: Sisli Hamidiye Etfal Training and Research Hospital
title: Effect of Resistance Exercises on Serum IGF-1 Levels in Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary:
Continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) is a type of positive airway pressure, where the air flow is introduced into the airways to maintain a continuous pressure to constantly stent the airways open, in people who are breathing spontaneously.

The application of CPAP maintains positive end expiratory pressure (PEEP), can decrease atelectasis, increases the surface area of the alveolus, improves V/Q matching, and hence, improves oxygenation.

Analgesia and sedation are essential components of care for critically ill patients, helping to relieve pain and anxiety, facilitate invasive procedures, reduce physiological stress and oxygen demand, and improve patient-ventilator synchrony. However, sedation practices vary considerably due to differences in institutional protocols, clinician preferences, and patient characteristics. Both inadequate and excessive sedation can adversely affect outcomes: untreated pain and agitation increase the sympathetic stress response, while oversedation is associated with prolonged mechanical ventilation, longer intensive care unit (ICU) stays, and a higher incidence of delirium and coma.

Combinations of propofol, benzodiazepines and opioids are frequently used for sedation. Opioids are usually added in painful procedures because benzodiazepines and propofol do not have any analgesic effect. However, opioid administration can lead to excessive sedation and some side effects.

Propofol (non-opioid, non-barbiturate, short-acting anesthetic agent) is popular in sedation because of its rapid induction and recovery times. However, its side effects, particularly cardiopulmonary depression, apnea and hypoventilation, have attracted attention to the search for alternatives.

Ketamine can be an alternative to opioids because it provides good analgesia even at low doses, sparing the respiratory and cardiovascular adverse effects of opioids. Unfortunately, its side effects (increased salivation, nausea, nightmares, delirium, and excitation) do not make it favorable as a single agent.

The past few years have carried increased interest in dexmedetomidine (a selective alpha-2 receptor agonist) in both anesthesia and intensive care. This alpha-2 receptor agonist has been used as the drug of choice for sedation in pediatric patients because of its lack of respiratory depressive effects, adequate sedative and analgesic action, and favorable antiarrhythmic effects.

Furthermore, minimizing benzodiazepine use and preferentially using propofol or dexmedetomidine to achieve appropriate sedation levels are associated with improved clinical outcomes.
interventions: Group DK will receive dexmedetomidine (0.2-1.4 μg/kg/hour) and ketamine (0.5 mg/kg/hr).
Group KP will receive dexmedetomidine (0.2-1.4 μg/kg/hour) and propofol (2-4 mg/kg/hr).(
primary_outcomes: The effect of each type of sedation on the outcome of the CPAP as for more compliant patient and lesser side effects
title: Dexametedomidine Ketamine Infusion Versus Dexametedomidine Propofol Infusion in Non-compliant Agitated Patients on Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) Mask Ventilation in the Intensive Care Unit

brief_summary:
This is an operational feasibility pilot preceding the main REFORM multi-site randomized controlled trial. Approximately 60 adults across three sites will be randomized equally to one of four remotely delivered audio-guided mental training programmes and will complete 12 sessions over approximately one month.

The purpose of the pilot is to assess the feasibility and functioning of the study procedures, including the Qualtrics survey and randomization workflow, participant adherence and experience, Camera HRV data collection and transfer, compensation procedures, and blinding materials.

Pilot outcomes will be summarized descriptively. The pilot is not designed for confirmatory efficacy testing. Pilot participants will be excluded from all confirmatory analyses of the subsequent main REFORM trial, and pilot data will not be used to calibrate the Bayesian stopping design, nuisance parameters, or Wave 1 recruitment target.
lead_sponsor: Institute for Human Development and Potential (IHDP), Singapore
title: Feasibility Pilot of Remote Mindfulness Training Across Multiple Sites (REFORM Pilot)

brief_summary: Spatial filtering is routinely required to reduce the statistical noise of gated SPECT myocardial perfusion imaging, but at the expense of image blurring. This study will evaluate a deep-learning-based noise reduction (DLNR) approach, developed to shorten acquisition times, when used as a replacement for conventional spatial filters (CSF).
primary_outcomes: Compare deep learning-based noise reduction and conventional spatial filters for myocardial scintigraphy image reconstruction.
title: Replacing Spatial Filtering With Deep-learning Noise Reduction

brief_summary:
This study will test whether electrical stimulation of the balance system adds benefit to an exercise program for adults aged 60 years and older. The treatment is called noisy electrical vestibular stimulation (nEVS). It uses low-level electrical current delivered through electrodes placed behind the ears and on the neck.

Participants who join the trial will be assigned by chance, in equal numbers, to active nEVS or sham nEVS. Sham sessions use the same equipment and preparation and will have no current delivered. Both groups will attend the RISE STRONG exercise program for 12 weeks. Exercise classes take place twice weekly and last about 35 to 45 minutes.

Participants will attend 18 active or sham sessions over six weeks. Each session lasts 20 minutes. Two sessions each week may take place on exercise days, and one additional weekly visit is expected. The stimulation course may take place during exercise weeks 1 to 6 or 7 to 12. Standing balance will be measured before and after the six-week course to compare the two groups. Other assessments examine walking, physical function, cognition, and self-reported health. The study will also record attendance, treatment completion, and adverse events.
title: EVS With Exercise for Balance With Older Adults

brief_summary: This study aims to examine the relationships between digital health literacy, diabetes distress, diabetes self-management, and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels in individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). The relationships between these variables will also be evaluated after controlling for relevant sociodemographic and clinical characteristics. The findings may contribute to a better understanding of factors associated with diabetes management and inform future nursing education and counseling interventions.
title: Digital Health Literacy and Diabetes Management in Type 2 Diabetes

brief_summary:
Malnutrition is a common comorbidity in patients undergoing thoracic surgery. Furthermore, chronic diseases, polypharmacy, low nutrient intake, reduced appetite, and psychological factors-all frequently observed in geriatric patients-serve as risk factors for the development of nutritional deficiencies. Consequently, it is crucial to address the issue of malnutrition in geriatric patients-who often present with these risk factors-and to ensure that a nutritional status assessment is performed prior to thoracic surgery. While numerous screening tools are currently available to assess nutritional status in the elderly, there is no established "gold standard." Although it has been suggested that these nutritional screening tools can serve as prognostic indicators for geriatric surgical patients, the relationship between these tools and postoperative outcomes-such as pain, complications, and length of hospital stay-has not yet been fully evaluated in geriatric patients undergoing lung resection. This study aims to determine the relationship between preoperative nutritional status and postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing lung resection-an area lacking sufficient literature-and to investigate whether preoperative nutritional support can reduce postoperative complications in this patient population.Patients will undergo preoperative assessment, and data regarding those meeting inclusion criteria will be recorded. This includes routine blood tests, age, height, body weight, BMI, gender, diagnoses, ASA and ARISCAT scores, the surgery performed, durations of surgery/anesthesia/one-lung ventilation, intraoperative fluids and IV agents administered, fluid balance, any complications arising during the procedure or postoperative follow-up (up to discharge), Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores at postoperative hours 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, and 24, Charlson Comorbidity Index, Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), and nutritional status (GNRI, NRS-2002, PNI, MNA-SF).

* Inclusion criteria: Patients undergoing elective thoracic surgery; patients undergoing lung resection via thoracotomy; patients who have provided informed consent; patients over 65 years of age; patients assessed as ASA class 1, 2, or 3; patients with a body mass index (BMI) between 18 and 35.
* Exclusion criteria: Patients with ASA class IV or higher; patients scheduled for emergency surgery; patients under 65 years of age; patients with a history of prior thoracic surgery; patients in GOLD groups 3 or 4; patients with systemic inflammatory disease; patients with preoperative chronic pain who regularly use anti-inflammatories/analgesics; patients with a history of pulmonary thromboembolism (PTE).
lead_sponsor: Ankara Ataturk Sanatorium Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: the correlation between preoperative nutritional status and postoperative results in geriatric patients undergoing lung resection by thoracotomy.
title: Preoperative Nutritional Status and Postoperative Outcomes in Geriatric Lung Resection
[Trial of device that is not approved or cleared by the U.S. FDA]

brief_summary:
Pediatric soft tissue sarcomas (STS) are a group of malignant tumors originating from primitive mesenchymal tissues and account for approximately 7% of childhood cancers. STS are broadly classified into rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) and non-rhabdomyosarcoma soft tissue sarcoma (NRSTS). RMS accounts for approximately one half of pediatric STS.

As reported, PAX fusion-positive RMS is more aggressive than fusion-negative RMS, with higher metastatic potential and poorer prognosis. Based on the unmet therapeutic need in pediatric sarcoma with PAX-family abnormalities, this study is intended to evaluate the preliminary safety and antitumor activity of entinostat with or without chemontherapy.
primary_outcomes: Safety: incidence of adverse events (AEs) and Grade ≥3 AEs according to NCI-CTCAE v5.0.
title: Preliminary Clinical Study of Entinostat in Children With Malignant Soft Tissue Sarcoma Harboring PAX-family Gene Abnormalities

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to learn which dose of study drug IBIO-610 has the right balance of safety, tolerability and impact on body composition in participants with obesity.
primary_outcomes: Assessment of the safety and tolerability of a single dose of IBIO-610; Incidence, severity, and relationship to study treatment of TEAEs and SAEs, as determined by clinical laboratory evaluations, vital signs, physical examinations, and ECGs.
title: A Study to Evaluate a Single Dose of IBIO-610 in Participant With Obesity.

brief_summary:
Hemorrhoid surgery is often followed by significant pain during the first few days after the operation. Pudendal nerve block is a pain-control technique that can help reduce discomfort after surgery. This study will compare two different methods of performing a pudendal nerve block: an ultrasound-guided method and a conventional landmark-guided method.

Patients undergoing Milligan-Morgan hemorrhoidectomy will be randomly assigned to one of the two techniques. The study will evaluate postoperative pain levels, pain medication use, treatment-related complications, and patient satisfaction.

The study hypothesis is that the ultrasound-guided technique may provide better pain relief and reduce the need for additional pain medication compared with the landmark-guided technique.
title: Ultrasound-Guided Versus Landmark-Guided Pudendal Block for Post-Hemorrhoidectomy Pain

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if using IC-ECG together with ultrasound works better than either method alone to identify the tip position of a PICC in adults with cancer. It will also learn about the safety and efficiency of the combined method.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the combined method confirm the correct PICC tip position more often than IC-ECG alone or ultrasound alone?

Does the combined method find PICC malposition more accurately?

Does the combined method take less time to complete tip positioning?

What medical problems do participants have during or after the procedure?

Researchers will compare three groups: IC-ECG alone, ultrasound alone, and IC-ECG plus ultrasound. A chest X-ray will be used as the standard check to see if the PICC tip is in the correct place.

Participants will:

Be adults with cancer who need a PICC.

Be assigned by chance to one of the three groups.

Have their PICC placed using the assigned tip-positioning method.

Have a chest X-ray as the usual standard check.

Allow the research team to record the procedure time, success, malposition, and any problems.

Not pay for the IC-ECG or ultrasound tip-positioning tests used in the study. Chest X-ray is part of usual care and will be charged as usual.

This study may help hospitals reduce routine X-ray use after PICC placement, lower radiation exposure, and make PICC placement safer and faster
interventions: Combined IC-ECG and Ultrasound PICC Tip Location Technique
title: IC ECG Combined With Ultrasound Bubble Test for PICC Tip Positioning Among Oncology Adults: A Three Arm Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to find out whether adding a human acellular dermal allograft (Dermis on Demand) during arthroscopic rotator cuff repair improves tendon-to-bone healing and lowers the rate of re-tear compared to standard repair alone. Sixty adults with large (3-5 cm) full-thickness superior or posterosuperior rotator cuff tears will be randomly assigned to repair with or without the allograft. Healing will be assessed by MRI at 12 months and by ultrasound at 6 months after surgery. Patient-reported outcomes, shoulder range of motion and strength, and operative time will also be compared between the groups.
interventions: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair; Biological: Dermis on Demand
title: Dermis on Demand Allograft Augmentation for Rotator Cuff Repair

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to evaluate neutrophil activation markers and circulating citrullinated histone H3 levels in adult patients with sepsis or septic shock.
title: Neutrophil Activation and NETosis in Sepsis

brief_summary:
Infectious endophthalmitis is a severe infection inside the eye that can rapidly cause permanent vision loss or loss of the eye. Standard treatment usually includes vitrectomy, a surgical procedure that removes infected vitreous gel, together with antibiotics. However, infection may remain difficult to control, particularly when the causative microorganism is unknown or resistant to commonly used antibiotics.

Povidone-iodine is a broad-spectrum antiseptic that acts rapidly against many types of bacteria, fungi, and other microorganisms. It is routinely used to disinfect the surface of the eye before surgery, but its use inside the eye for treating established infection is still investigational.

The purpose of this study is to determine whether brief irrigation of the vitreous cavity with a low concentration of povidone-iodine can improve infection control when added to standard vitrectomy and antimicrobial treatment. The main question is whether irrigation with povidone-iodine containing 0.0025% available iodine increases the proportion of patients whose infection is controlled by 14 days without silicone oil tamponade, compared with irrigation using standard balanced salt solution alone.

This is a single-center, prospective, randomized, parallel-group clinical study involving approximately 38 patients with infectious endophthalmitis. Participants will be assigned in a 1:1 ratio according to the severity of inflammation at enrollment. After vitrectomy has been completed, patients in the study group will receive vitreous cavity irrigation with povidone-iodine containing 0.0025% available iodine for 2 minutes. The solution will then be removed from the eye. Patients in the control group will undergo the same surgical procedure using balanced salt solution without povidone-iodine. Both groups will otherwise receive appropriate standard antimicrobial treatment and clinical care.

The study hypothesis is that brief exposure to low-concentration povidone-iodine will rapidly reduce the number of microorganisms remaining in the eye and improve infection control without causing clinically significant damage to the retina, cornea, or other eye structures.

In addition to the primary outcome of infection control at Day 14 without silicone oil tamponade, the study will evaluate several secondary outcomes，including changes in best-corrected visual acuity, the need for additional eye surgery, and vision-related quality of life. Safety outcomes will include changes in retinal function measured by electroretinography, retinal structure assessed by optical coherence tomography, corneal endothelial cell density, intraocular pressure, and the occurrence and severity of adverse events throughout follow-up.
interventions: Povidone-iodine intravitreal irrigation with povidone-iodine containing 0.0025% available iodine
primary_outcomes: Infection control rate without silicone oil tamponade
title: Vitrectomy Combined With Povidone-Iodine Vitreous Irrigation for Infectious Endophthalmitis

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to document clinical outcomes after primary hip arthroscopy in patients with femoroacetabular impingement, describe the pathology zone distribution and detect whether the pathology site impact the outcomes. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does hip-related quality of life improve from before surgery to 12 months after surgery?
* Where inside the hip joint (front, mixed, or back) does cartilage and labral damage most commonly occur in patients undergoing arthroscopy for FAI?
* Do pain and quality-of-life outcomes at 12 months differ between patients based on the hip damage region?

Participants will

* Complete questionnaires about hip pain and function (iHOT-12, a pain scale, and a quality-of-life questionnaire) before surgery
* Undergo standard hip arthroscopy, during which the surgeon will record the exact location and grade of any joint damage found
* Complete the same questionnaires again 12 months after surgery
primary_outcomes: Change in iHOT-12 from baseline to 12 months for the whole cohort
title: Mapping Joint Damage Patterns in Femoroacetabular Impingement

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate MyDiet, a nutrition education app designed to improve nutrition knowledge among healthcare providers. In this randomized trial, participants will be assigned to one of two groups: an intervention group or a control crossover group. Participants in the intervention group will have access to the app for two months, while those in the control crossover group will receive access during the second month of their participation.

The study will evaluate whether the app improves nutrition knowledge, has the potential to influence dietary behaviours, and supports healthcare providers in strengthening their ability to provide nutrition-related advice to their patients.
title: Health Care Professionals Diet App Study

brief_summary: This clinical trial studies whether a community based intervention improves cervical cancer screening (CCS) among women in the Hispanic and East African immigrant community. Previous research has shown that CCS remains low among women of the Hispanic and East African immigrant community due to lack of awareness about cervical cancer as well as recommended screening guidelines. The community based intervention in this trial will offer CCS in the Hispanic and East African immigrant community using a test that can be completed by the individual. The test uses a brush that is placed inside the vagina to collect a sample. The self-collected sample is then tested for a virus called human papillomavirus (HPV). Because some types of HPV can cause cervical cancer, checking for HPV, may lower a woman's chance of getting cervical cancer. A community based intervention may be an effective way to improve CCS among women in the Hispanic and East African immigrant community.
interventions: Receive recommended steps following abnormal results
primary_outcomes: Number of individuals screened in the community via this protocol
title: A Community Based Intervention to Improve Cervical Cancer Screening Among Women in the Hispanic and East African Immigrant Community

brief_summary:
Cerebral venous thrombosis (CVT) is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening type of stroke, predominantly affecting young adults and women. Although prompt diagnosis and anticoagulant therapy can lead to favorable outcomes, data regarding the clinical spectrum, neuroimaging patterns, risk factors, and long-term functional recovery of CVT patients in central Vietnam remain limited.

This prospective observational study aims to establish a hospital-based registry to investigate the clinical characteristics, neuroimaging features, etiology, and treatment outcomes of patients diagnosed with cerebral venous thrombosis at Danang Hospital.

All consecutive patients with confirmed CVT admitted to Danang Hospital are enrolled and managed according to standard clinical protocols. Participants are monitored throughout their hospital stay to assess acute manifestations, imaging abnormalities (on CT/CTV or MRI/MRV), and inpatient complications. Functional outcomes and recovery are evaluated at hospital discharge and during follow-up using the modified Rankin Scale (mRS).
primary_outcomes: Favorable Functional Outcome Assessed by the Modified Rankin Scale (mRS)
title: Danang Cerebral Venous Thrombosis Registry

brief_summary:
This study aims to determine whether preoperative patient education prepared with the assistance of artificial intelligence can reduce lung complications after major abdominal surgery in older patients.

A total of 242 patients will be randomly assigned to an education group or a usual care group. Patients in the education group will receive education from a researcher at least 24 hours before surgery, using educational materials developed with artificial intelligence and reviewed by experts. Their questions will be answered, and they will receive a printed copy of the educational material. Patients in the usual care group will receive standard nursing care.

Both groups will be assessed before surgery and on postoperative days 1, 3, 7, and 30. Follow-up assessments will be conducted face-to-face during hospitalization and by telephone after discharge. The researcher assessing postoperative complications will not know which group patients have been assigned to. The occurrence of postoperative lung complications will be compared between the two groups.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With at Least One Postoperative Pulmonary Complication
title: AI-Assisted Education Before Surgery to Prevent Lung Complications in Older Surgical Patients

brief_summary: Neoadjuvant immunotherapy combined with chemotherapy followed by surgery has become an important treatment strategy for resectable non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, patients who do not achieve a pathological complete response (non-pCR) after neoadjuvant treatment remain at a high risk of disease recurrence, and optimal postoperative adjuvant treatment for these patients remains unclear. Adebrelimab, an immune checkpoint inhibitor targeting PD-L1, and famitinib, a multitarget tyrosine kinase inhibitor with antiangiogenic activity, may have complementary antitumor effects. Therefore, we conduct this prospective, single-arm, phase II clinical trial to investigate the efficacy and safety of adebrelimab combined with famitinib as postoperative adjuvant therapy in patients with resectable NSCLC who did not achieve pCR after neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy followed by surgery.
title: Adebrelimab Plus Famitinib as Adjuvant Therapy in Non-pCR NSCLC

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of gamified home-based core neuromuscular training on pain intensity, functional disability, core muscular endurance, and exercise adherence in women with chronic nonspecific low back pain. Participants will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either a gamified intervention group or a non-gamified control group. Both groups will perform the same progressive core exercise program. The intervention group will use a digital application with gamification features, while the control group will perform the exercises without gamification. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, week 3, and week 6. The study will determine whether gamification provides additional benefits over conventional home-based exercise in improving clinical outcomes and exercise adherence in women with chronic nonspecific low back pain.
conditions: Low Back Pain and Core Muscle
interventions: Gamified Intervention Group: core neuromuscular exercise program using a digital application with gamification features
title: Gamified Home-Based Core Neuromuscular Training for Chronic Low Back Pain

brief_summary: "This prospective observational study aims to evaluate the prognostic value of dynamic changes in the serum uric acid-to-albumin ratio (UAR) measured on admission (Day 0) and on Day 3, along with mNUTRIC and PNI scores, regarding 28-day mortality in intensive care patients aged 65 and older."
interventions: Uric Acid to Albumin Ratio (UAR) and Nutritional Risk Scores
title: Dynamic Inflammatory Changes and Nutritional Risk Scores in ICU Patients Aged 65 Years and Older

brief_summary: Although the benefits of adapted physical activity (APA) are well documented in the scientific literature, few studies have specifically examined the impact of adapted boxing on body image and self-esteem in patients with haematological conditions. The current approach relies on the empirical observations of healthcare professionals, but no systematic evaluation has been conducted to quantify the actual effects of this practice on patients. This project therefore aims to address this lack of data by rigorously and scientifically assessing the impact of a boxing session on patients' psychological and emotional well-being. The use of validated questionnaires (Rosenberg Scale, QIC, EORTC QLQ-C30) will provide objective and comparable measures12.
primary_outcomes: Change in Body Image Score Assessed Using the QIC Questionnaire
Patients' Perceptions of Body Image Assessed Through Semi-Structured Interviews
title: Adapted Boxing and Photography in Haematology: Body Image and Self-Esteem

brief_summary:
The SURGUT study aims to assess how well a computer model predicts bowel leaks after surgery. It will also examine whether adding surgeons' intuition improves these predictions.

The study will include adults having surgery to remove part of the colon or rectum. During the operation, the remaining bowel ends are joined together. Sometimes, this connection does not heal properly and a leak develops. This is called an anastomotic leak and can cause serious complications.

The research questions are:

* How well does a previously developed computer model predict a leak within 30 days after surgery?
* How accurately do surgeons estimate the risk of a leak?
* Does combining the computer model with surgeons' assessments improve prediction compared with the model alone?

This observational study will take place at several hospitals in different countries. Researchers will collect information about participants' health, surgery, and presence of complications. Surgeons will complete a pre-operative and an immediately post-operative questionnaire about the estimated risk of a leak, surgical difficulty, and concerns about the bowel connection.

Researchers will record whether a leak occurs within 30 days after surgery. They will compare these outcomes with the predictions from the computer model, surgeons' assessments, and the combination of both.

The findings may help improve how clinicians identify people at higher risk of a leak after bowel surgery.
primary_outcomes: Discriminative performance of the machine learning model for predicting anastomotic leakage
title: Surgical Intuition in Anastomotic Leakage After Colorectal Surgery

brief_summary: Blood pressure medications may provide limited benefit and cause side effects in frail older adults. It is unclear how best to stop these medications. Guidelines often recommend gradually reducing the dose, but this process can be time-consuming. This study examined the feasibility of stopping blood pressure medications without gradually reducing the dose in long-term care residents with low blood pressure. Eligible residents had their medication stopped and were monitored for four weeks.
title: Stopping Blood Pressure Medications Without Tapering in Long-Term Care

brief_summary: Arterial catheterization provides continuous blood pressure monitoring and repeated blood sampling in children undergoing surgery at high cardiovascular or hemorrhagic risk, and in critically ill children. The radial artery is the conventional site, but cannulation remains challenging in children because of small vessel caliber and frequent anatomical variants. Ultrasound guidance has made alternative sites accessible, and the ulnar artery has a comparable caliber and a depth often closer to the range considered optimal for puncture. This trial compared ultrasound-guided ulnar versus radial arterial cannulation in children older than one year, with regard to first-attempt success and the rate of local complications.
primary_outcomes: Successful arterial cannulation at the first attempt
title: Ultrasound-Guided Ulnar Versus Radial Artery Cannulation in Children

brief_summary: The ORION study will evaluate a novel treatment approach for patients with recurrent, metastatic, oligometastatic, or locoregionally incurable head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). Participants will receive pulsed adaptive radiotherapy delivered in 3 to 5 treatment courses approximately 10 days apart, alongside standard-of-care pembrolizumab with or without chemotherapy. Using advanced imaging and adaptive treatment planning, radiotherapy will be tailored to changes in tumor size and surrounding tissues throughout treatment. The study will assess safety, disease control, progression-free survival, quality of life, and biological markers of treatment response. Researchers hypothesize that combining pulsed radiotherapy with systemic therapy will improve 12-month progression-free survival from 17% to 32%, potentially leading to improved outcomes for patients with advanced head and neck cancer.
conditions: Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma (HNSCC)
interventions: Pulsed Adaptive Radiotherapy Combined with Pembrolizumab with or without chemotherapy
title: Optimizing Response to Immunotherapy With Online Adaptive Pulsed Radiotherapy in Incurable Head and Neck Cancers

brief_summary:
The active phase of labor is a critical period for the progress of labor and maternal comfort. Non-pharmacological interventions such as birth ball exercises are frequently used to support labor progress and maternal mobility. Birth ball exercises may facilitate fetal descent, improve maternal pelvic mobility, and potentially shorten labor duration.

Intrapartum ultrasound has recently emerged as an objective method for assessing labor progress and fetal head position. Compared with digital vaginal examination, intrapartum ultrasound provides more reliable and reproducible measurements.

The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of birth ball exercises performed during the active phase of labor on labor progress using intrapartum ultrasound. The findings of this study may contribute to understanding the potential benefits of birth ball exercises in supporting physiological labor.
primary_outcomes: Angle of Progression (AoP) during the active phase of labor
Head-Perineum Distance (HPD) during the active phase of labor
Progression Distance (PD) during the active phase of labor
Fetal Head Direction (HD) during the active phase of labor
Fetal Head Position during the active phase of labor
title: Effect of Birth Ball Exercise on Labor Progress During the Active Phase of Labor Assessed by Intrapartum Ultrasound

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate how safe Opsynvi (macitentan/tadalafil fixed-dose combination) is in adult participants with pulmonary arterial hypertension under routine clinical practice in Korea. Pulmonary arterial hypertension is a condition where the blood vessels that carry blood from the heart to the lungs become narrowed or stiff.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With Adverse Events (AEs)
Number of Participants With Adverse Drug Reactions (ADRs)
Number of Participants With Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
Number of Participants With Serious Adverse Drug Reactions (SADRs)
Number of Participants With Unlisted AE, ADR, SAE, and SADR
title: A Study of Opsynvi in Adults Participants With Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension in Korea

brief_summary: This is a Phase I/II study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of autologous T cells engineered with a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) targeting CD19 in adult patients with relapsed or refractory (r/r) B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL).
conditions: Relapsed or Refractory B Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia
lead_sponsor: Hospital Universitario Dr. Jose E. Gonzalez
primary_outcomes: Incidence of dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) and determination of the recommended Phase II dose (RP2D)
Frequency and severity of adverse events (AEs) and serious adverse events (SAEs)
title: CD19 CAR-T Cell Therapy in Adults With Relapsed or Refractory B-Cell Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia: A Phase I/II Study

brief_summary:
Urothelial carcinoma is the most common cancer of the urinary system. It includes bladder cancer and upper urinary tract cancer, which starts in the kidney pelvis or ureter. Doctors currently tell these types apart mainly by using invasive tests such as cystoscopy or ureteroscopy. These tests can be uncomfortable and may miss some tumors. This study is testing whether a urine sample can offer a simpler, non-invasive way to detect urothelial cancer and identify where the cancer started.

This is a prospective, multicenter, observational study. It plans to enroll 477 adults, including 159 patients with upper urinary tract urothelial cancer, 159 patients with bladder cancer, and 159 people without cancer. Participants will provide a midstream urine sample of about 30 mL using a special collection tube. No experimental drug or device will be given. Participants will receive their usual medical care.

The urine samples will be sent to a central laboratory. Researchers will extract cell-free DNA, which are small pieces of DNA released by cells into the urine. They will then perform low-pass whole-genome sequencing and study DNA fragment patterns, called fragmentomics. Machine learning will be used to build models that may help detect urothelial cancer and distinguish upper urinary tract cancer from bladder cancer. The study will also explore whether these urine DNA patterns are related to tumor stage and grade. The results may help develop a convenient urine-based test for patients in the future.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Receiver Operating Characteristic Curve for Differentiating Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma from Lower Tract Urothelial Carcinoma
title: Urinary Cell-Free DNA Liquid Biopsy for Urothelial Cancer Diagnosis and Origin Identification

brief_summary: The purpose of the study is to evaluate the safety and feasibility of daily-adaptive post-prostatectomy stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) to the prostate fossa in men undergoing salvage radiotherapy after radical prostatectomy.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of grade ≥3 treatment-related GU/GI toxicity
title: SURPASS: Stereotactic Ultra-hypofractionated Radiotherapy for Post-prostatectomy Patients: Adaptive Salvage SBRT

brief_summary:
Dietary patterns may influence maternal inflammatory status and pregnancy outcomes. However, structured anti-inflammatory dietary interventions specifically designed for pregnant women remain limited. This study aims to develop and evaluate an evidence-based, theory-informed anti-inflammatory dietary intervention to improve dietary habits and reduce dietary inflammatory potential during pregnancy.

The intervention will be developed through evidence synthesis, qualitative research, and expert consultation, guided by the the Behaviour Change Wheel. Following intervention development, a randomized controlled trial will be conducted to assess its feasibility, acceptability, and preliminary effects. Pregnant women will be randomly assigned to an intervention group receiving individualized anti-inflammatory dietary guidance and behavioral support or a control group receiving routine antenatal care. Outcomes will include intervention feasibility, dietary inflammatory potential, maternal inflammatory biomarkers, and relevant pregnancy-related outcomes. The findings will inform further refinement of the intervention and provide evidence for future research.
primary_outcomes: Change in Dietary Inflammatory Index (DII) Score
title: Pregnancy Anti-inflammatory Diet Intervention Study

brief_summary: This study aims to Develop a low-cost, PRO-based ML tool can: - Reduce lab costs - Enable telemedicine monitoring - Detect flares early - Improve care in resource-limited settings.
primary_outcomes: Develop a low-cost, PRO-based ML tool.
title: Prediction of SLE Flares Using Patient-Reported Outcomes and Machine Learning

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate and compare three different management strategies for benign breast fibroadenoma: conservative management with clinical and radiological follow-up (observation), ultrasound-guided percutaneous microwave ablation (MWA), and conventional open surgical excision.

Fibroadenoma is the most common benign solid breast tumor in young women. While conventional surgical excision provides complete tissue removal, it may result in visible surgical scars, breast volume loss, and contour deformity. Minimally invasive thermal techniques such as microwave ablation offer potential advantages in tissue preservation and cosmetic satisfaction under local anesthesia. This study aims to assess and compare the therapeutic success, safety, postoperative pain, recovery period, complication rates, and cosmetic outcomes among female patients undergoing these three approaches at Sohag University Hospital.
title: Management of Breast Fibroadenoma: Comparing Observation, Microwave Ablation, and Surgical Excision

brief_summary: This is a phase II, open-label, single-arm, exploratory study to evaluate the intracranial arterial recanalization of multiple doses of LT3001 drug product in participant with acute ischemic stroke (AIS)
primary_outcomes: The rate of successful recanalization at 24 hours after the 1st IP. Successful recanalization is defined as any improvement in Arterial Occlusive Lesion (AOL) score.
title: A Study to Evaluate the Intracranial Arterial Recanalization With Multiple Doses of LT3001 Drug Product in AIS Participant

brief_summary:
This is a single-country, retrospective, observational biomarker study conducted in Greece to evaluate Folate Receptor Alpha (FRα) expression in patients with high-grade serous ovarian, fallopian tube, and primary peritoneal cancer at the time of diagnosis. Approximately 200 eligible female patients (≥18 years) diagnosed between 1 January 2001 and 30 July 2025 will be included from around 15 clinical sites affiliated with the Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group.

Historically collected Formalin-Fixed Paraffin-Embedded (FFPE) tissue samples stored in the Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group biobank will be analyzed centrally using the Ventana FOLR1 RxDx assay to determine FRα expression. Only samples collected at initial diagnosis will be included; relapse samples will be excluded.

The primary objective is to assess the prevalence of FRα-positive status, defined as ≥75% viable tumor cells with moderate (2+) and/or strong (3+) membrane staining. Secondary objectives include evaluation of intra-tumoral heterogeneity, concordance between primary and metastatic lesions, prevalence of lower FRα expression levels, and associations between FRα expression and clinical characteristics, BRCA/HRD status, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS).

All analyses will be descriptive, with additional exploratory statistical methods including chi-square tests, Cohen's kappa, correlation analyses, ANOVA, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, and Cox proportional hazards models. Data will be retrospectively collected from the Hellenic Cooperative Oncology Group registry and medical records and entered into a secure REDCap eCRF system.
title: Folate Receptor Alpha (FRα) Expression and Heterogeneity in Epithelial Ovarian Cancer

brief_summary:
The aim of this randomized controlled study is to evaluate the effects of a six-week low-fermentable oligosaccharides, disaccharides, monosaccharides, and polyols (FODMAP) diet on gastrointestinal symptoms, inflammatory biomarkers, nutritional status, and quality of life in pediatric and adult patients with Fabry disease.

A total of 30 patients with genetically or laboratory-confirmed Fabry disease are planned to be enrolled and randomly assigned to either an intervention group receiving an individualized low-FODMAP diet or a control group continuing their habitual diet. Assessments will be conducted at baseline and after six weeks. Gastrointestinal symptoms, stool characteristics, quality of life, anthropometric measurements, body composition, dietary intake, and biochemical parameters, including inflammatory biomarkers, will be evaluated.

The study aims to investigate whether a low-FODMAP diet may provide additional benefits in managing gastrointestinal manifestations and inflammation in patients with Fabry disease.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gastrointestinal Symptom Rating Scale (GSRS) Score
Change in Tumor Necrosis Factor-alpha (TNF-α) Levels
title: Evaluation of the Effect of a Low-FODMAP Diet on Gastrointestinal Symptoms and Inflammatory Markers in Fabry Patients

brief_summary:
This study tests whether certain medicines and a skin treatment can slow down or partly reverse the body's aging process.

As people age, the activity of their genes changes in predictable ways. Researchers can now measure a person's "biological age" from these gene-activity patterns in skin and blood. This study uses that measurement to see whether treatment can lower a person's biological age compared with their own starting point.

Adults in the study take geroprotective ("age-protecting") agents by mouth or by injection. A separate skin serum containing small anti-aging peptides is applied to certain areas of skin, and those treated areas are compared with untreated areas on the same person.

Skin and blood samples are taken at set times to measure biological age and markers of cell aging before, during, and after treatment. The main goal is to find out whether treatment lowers measured biological age in skin and blood. The study also looks at whether the treatments are safe and well tolerated.
lead_sponsor: Frontiers in Bioscience Research Institute and Aging
primary_outcomes: START/REST biological age (transcriptomic tAge and proteomic pAge), in years
title: Systemic and Topical Geroprotective Rejuvenation Assessed by START/REST Aging Clocks

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if low-dose esketamine combined with dexmedetomidine can reduce chronic pain after pancreatic surgery in adults. It will also learn about its safety. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does low-dose esketamine combined with dexmedetomidine lower the number of participants who have chronic pain 3 months after pancreatic surgery?
* What medical problems do participants have when receiving this treatment? Researchers will compare low-dose esketamine combined with dexmedetomidine to a control group (saline placebo during surgery and standard sufentanil patient-controlled intravenous analgesia after surgery) to see if the study treatment reduces chronic pain after pancreatic surgery. This is a two-center randomized controlled trial. About 450 adults will be enrolled and randomly assigned to the treatment group or the control group.

Participants will:

* Be adults aged 18 years or older, weigh at least 40 kg, and be scheduled for elective pancreatic surgery, including pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure), pancreatectomy, or distal pancreatectomy.
* Receive the study drugs or placebo during surgery and use a patient-controlled intravenous pain pump after surgery.
* Be followed for up to 3 months after surgery to check for chronic pain.
lead_sponsor: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Chronic Pain at 3 Months After Pancreatic Surgery
title: Effect of Low-Dose Esketamine Combined With Dexmedetomidine on the Incidence of Chronic Postsurgical Pain in Patients Undergoing Pancreatic Surgery

brief_summary:
Some people feel pain after a root canal treatment. This study will test whether intracanal cryotherapy, a final rinse of the tooth with cold sterile saline, can reduce this pain compared with a room-temperature rinse.

Previous studies have suggested that intracanal cryotherapy may reduce pain after root canal treatment. In this study, we will examine its effect in a defined group of patients and explore how it works. We will measure the level of irisin, a substance with reported anti-inflammatory properties, in saliva to see whether cryotherapy changes it. We will also look at whether a person's tendency to worry about pain (pain catastrophizing) changes the effect of cryotherapy on pain, and whether dental anxiety is related to pain after treatment.

Adults aged 18 to 65 who need root canal treatment on a single-rooted lower premolar tooth will receive standard single-visit treatment. By chance, 100 participants will be placed in a cold-saline group or a room-temperature-saline group. Thirty healthy volunteers will give one saliva sample for comparison. Participants will complete questionnaires before treatment, rate their pain over the 7 days after treatment, and give saliva samples for irisin measurement.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does intracanal cryotherapy lower pain after root canal treatment? Does it change salivary irisin levels? Does pain catastrophizing change the effect of cryotherapy? Is dental anxiety related to pain after treatment?
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain as Assessed by Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
title: Effect of Intracanal Cryotherapy on Pain, Anxiety, and Salivary Irisin After Root Canal Treatment

brief_summary: The purpose of this multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase IIb clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of intravenous hBMMSC injection in patients with autoimmune pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (aPAP).
interventions: The human Bone Marrow Mesenchymal Stem Cell (hBMMSC) injection
title: A Study of hBMMSC Injection in Patients With aPAP

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a new 1% Phenytoin mucoadhesive film is safe and works to treat oral ulcers in healthy adult volunteers and patients with oral ulcers.

The main questions it aims to answer are the following:

Is the 1% Phenytoin film safe and well-tolerated when placed on oral ulcers? Does the film reduce pain and improve ulcer healing compared to a blank film?

Researchers will compare participants receiving the 1% Phenytoin mucoadhesive film to those receiving a blank (placebo) film to see if the active film improves healing and reduces pain.

Participants will:

Have the assigned film placed directly over their oral ulcer once daily for 7 consecutive days.

Attend regular clinic visits for check-ups, including blood tests and monitoring of ulcer appearance, body weight, and food intake.

Report any pain, discomfort, or changes in their condition to the research team.
lead_sponsor: Misr University for Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Treatment-Emergent Adverse Events (Safety and Tolerability)
title: A Study of Phenytoin Mucoadhesive Film for Oral Ulcers in Healthy Volunteers

brief_summary: Percutaneous nephrolithotomy (PCNL) is an established intervention for large or ESWL-resistant renal stones in pediatric populations. While traditionally performed in the prone position, the supine position offers potential advantages, including simpler patient positioning, easier airway management, better ergonomics, and shorter operative duration. This prospective randomized trial compares the safety, efficacy, operative time, complication rates, and stone-free rates between supine and prone mini-percutaneous nephrolithotripsy (Mini-PCNL) in children under 15 years of age presenting with single renal stones measuring 10 to 30 mm.
title: Supine vs. Prone Mini-PCNL in Children

brief_summary: This is a prospective, observational, multi-center cohort study of pediatric cardiac arrests. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the physiologic response to epinephrine as an outcome discriminator in pediatric in-hospital cardiac arrest (IHCA). In addition, the investigators will determine optimal epinephrine dosing strategies based on the initial physiologic response to epinephrine, and to develop machine learning (ML) algorithms to guide intra-arrest therapy.
primary_outcomes: Return of Spontaneous Circulation (ROSC) lasting 20 minutes
title: Physiology-directed Epinephrine Dosing in Pediatric Cardiac Arrest

brief_summary: Preclinical evidence indicates that IL-1 inflammatory signaling suppresses bone marrow mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) from secreting stem cell factor (SCF), leading to failure of their hematopoietic supportive capacity, and that the interleukin-1 receptor antagonist (IL-1Ra, Anakinra) can reverse this process. Sustained low-level IL-1 signaling also drives hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) dysfunction, including progression of clonal hematopoiesis and transformation to myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or acute myeloid leukemia (AML). A prior phase 2 trial of IL-1 inhibition in lower-risk MDS demonstrated hematologic improvement without an increased risk of leukemic transformation. Based on these findings, this study hypothesizes that early administration of Anakinra after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT) in patients with MDS, by inhibiting IL-1β signaling, improving the bone marrow microenvironment, and reducing the occurrence of poor graft function (PGF), does not increase the risk of post-transplant relapse. The study comprises two parts: a dose-escalation phase to determine the maximum tolerated dose (MTD) / recommended phase 2 dose (RP2D) of Anakinra in post-allo-HSCT patients, and an efficacy-validation phase to evaluate the preventive effect of Anakinra at the RP2D on PGF.
primary_outcomes: incidence of poor graft function (PGF) by Day +100
title: Anakinra for Prevention of Poor Graft Function in MDS Allo-HSCT

brief_summary:
The EURO-APPLEBY Registry is a prospective, multicenter European observational registry designed to characterize contemporary surgical practice and evaluate perioperative and long-term oncological outcomes in patients undergoing distal pancreatectomy with celiac axis resection (DP-CAR), also known as the modified Appleby procedure, for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma of the body and/or tail.

Consecutive eligible patients undergoing elective DP-CAR with curative intent will be prospectively enrolled at participating European hepatopancreatobiliary centers over a 24-month recruitment period. Clinical, treatment-related, imaging, operative, pathological, postoperative, and follow-up data will be collected using standardized definitions and a harmonized electronic case report form.

The primary objectives are to characterize postoperative morbidity and mortality, overall survival, and disease-free survival following DP-CAR. Secondary objectives include identifying factors associated with postoperative ischemic complications and oncological outcomes, evaluating the impact of neoadjuvant therapy and surgical approaches, and assessing variability in clinical practice and outcomes across participating centers.

This observational registry will not modify routine clinical care. The findings are expected to support benchmarking, improve patient selection and perioperative management, and inform the development of evidence-based European recommendations for DP-CAR.
title: European Appleby Registry for Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary: Upper extremity (UE) paresis or weakness is one of the most frequent impairments after stroke. Despite intense rehabilitation, motor and functional recovery of patients with severe hand impairments is poor. Hence, there is a need for more effective treatments to enhance motor function in patients with severe hand impairments after stroke. Adaptive functional electrical stimulation (FES) appears to be a promising treatment and has the potential to facilitate active movement in individuals with severe impairments post-stroke. In addition, transcranial random noise stimulation (trns) is a widely studied, non-invasive and safe method to enhance the corticomotor excitability in individuals with chronic stroke. However, the effect of combining trns and adaptive FES in patients with severe hand impairments has not been investigated. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to investigate whether combining trns with FES will enhance hand function in individuals with chronic stroke than FES alone. The investigators predict that combining trns with FES will significantly enhance hand function than FES alone.
primary_outcomes: Stroke Impact Scale - Hand Function Score
Transcranial Magnetic stimulation-induced motor evoked potential
title: A Novel Multimodal Approach to Promote Motor Recovery and Plasticity After Stroke

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate the association between full-arch implant-supported fixed dental rehabilitation and changes in biological aging among adults with complete tooth loss (edentulism).

A total of 60 adults aged 50 years or older with complete tooth loss will be enrolled in this prospective cohort study. Participants will be included in one of two groups: an implant rehabilitation group (30 participants) receiving full-arch implant-supported fixed dental prostheses, and a delayed-treatment comparison group (30 participants) receiving the same treatment after a three-month delay.

The main outcome is the change in biological age estimated from DNA methylation in saliva samples, compared with chronological age. Other outcomes include facial biological age, physical frailty, quality of life, nutritional status, emotional well-being, cognitive function, and brain function.

Participants will undergo assessments at baseline and at 3, 12, and 24 months. These assessments will include saliva collection, facial photographs and scans, physical function tests, questionnaires, cognitive tests, and brain function measurements using electroencephalography (EEG), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).

The study will examine whether changes in oral function following implant-supported fixed dental rehabilitation are associated with changes in biological aging and brain function. The findings may improve understanding of the relationship between oral rehabilitation and overall health in older adults with complete tooth loss.
primary_outcomes: Change in Salivary DNA Methylation Age Acceleration
title: Biological Aging Following Full-Arch Implant-Supported Fixed Rehabilitation in Edentulous Patients

brief_summary:
Subclinical depression - depressive symptoms that fall below the threshold for major depressive disorder - is common in young adults and predicts later depressive episodes, yet it often goes untreated. This study tests whether a brief, remotely delivered non-deceptive (open-label) placebo intervention reduces subclinical depressive symptoms over approximately two weeks.

Participants aged 18-30 living in Ohio, with PHQ-8 scores in the 5-9 range, are randomly assigned to one of three groups: a non-deceptive placebo group, a blinded control group, or an unblinded control group. All participants complete three remote sessions over 16-18 days and complete the same assessments on the same schedule. Participants in the non-deceptive placebo group additionally receive psychoeducation about placebo effects and placebo pills that are explicitly described as containing no active ingredients, which they take twice daily for two weeks. Participants in the unblinded control group are told they have been assigned to a control condition. Participants in the blinded control group are not told their group assignment until debriefing at the end of the study.

The study has two aims. The first is to estimate the effect of the non-deceptive placebo intervention on depressive symptoms and related outcomes. The second is methodological: to determine whether telling control participants that they are in a control group changes their outcomes, and therefore whether the choice of control condition systematically biases estimates of non-deceptive placebo effects.
title: Testing a Non-Deceptive Placebo Intervention for Subclinical Depressive Symptoms

brief_summary:
In recent years, evaluating cardiac function with magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has drawn widespread interest. However, cardiac MRI is prone to severe motion artifacts from cardiac contraction, frequently requiring complex triggering procedures to enhance image quality-a task that typically demands a highly skilled technologist to execute within limited clinical time. As there is currently no optimized cardiac MRI protocol at Chang Gung Memorial Hospital, this subproject aims to first establish a clinically feasible, optimized protocol to support other subprojects and future studies. The investigators will develop a standard operating procedure (SOP) and subsequently use it to evaluate recovery in heart failure patients.

Over this three-year project, the investigators plan to use MRI to evaluate cardiac morphology and function in heart failure patients. In Year 1, the investigators will establish a clinically feasible protocol to assess myocardial stability; baseline images from healthy controls will be incorporated into the integrated project. In Year 2, the investigators will introduce accelerated imaging techniques, assess the correlation between disease severity and MRI findings, and measure cardiac diffusion parameters. In Year 3, the investigators will follow heart failure patients to monitor their recovery process.
title: The Development and Optimization of a Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Imaging Protocol in a 3 Tesla Scanner

brief_summary: This study is a randomized, double-blind, dose-escalation, placebo-controlled Phase I clinical trial in healthy participants to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of single intravenous and subcutaneous administrations of SHR-3201.
title: A Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics of SHR 3201 Injection in Healthy Participants

brief_summary: Upper-limb spasticity and impaired hand function are experienced by up to 70% of stroke survivors, which significantly restricts their independence in fulfilling daily activities. This research aims to assess whether combining TECAR therapy with FES produces superior improvements in hand function compared to FES alone in stroke patients with upper-limb spasticity.
title: TECAR and FES for Hand Function in Post-Stroke Spasticity

brief_summary: This is a Phase 1b, 2-part, multi-center, open-label study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, dosimetry, and pharmacokinetics (PK) of \[64Cu\]Cu-AKY-2519 and/or \[225Ac\]Ac-AKY-2519, as well as the preliminary anti-tumor activity of \[225Ac\]Ac-AKY-2519 in participants with B7-H3 imaging positive solid tumors.
conditions: Small Cell Lung Cancer Extensive Stage
Head Neck Cancer Squamous Cell Metastatic
primary_outcomes: Part 1: Occurrence of adverse events by severity and occurrence of serious adverse events (SAEs) in participants who received [225Ac]Ac-AKY-2519

brief_summary: Melasma is a common acquired hyperpigmentation disorder that significantly affects quality of life. Various topical agents are used in its treatment, including Vitamin C and Niacinamide, both of which possess depigmenting properties. This randomized controlled trial aims to compare the efficacy of topical Vitamin C and topical Niacinamide in patients with melasma. A total of 100 patients will be enrolled and randomly allocated into two groups. Treatment efficacy will be assessed using the Melasma Area and Severity Index (MASI) score after 12 weeks of therapy. The findings of this study may help determine the more effective topical treatment option for melasma.
title: COMPARISON OF TOPICAL VITAMIN C VS NIACINAMIDE IN TREATMENT OF MELASMA

brief_summary:
This is a prospective, non-randomized, single arm, single center feasibility study to investigate surgical feasibility and technical success of robotic treatment for Median Arcuate Ligament Syndrome using the Intuitive Da Vinci Single Port Robot.

This study aims to systematically collect and analyze data on patient demographics, operative details, postoperative complications, length of hospital stay, and overall recovery times following vascular surgery robotic-assisted procedures. By establishing a comprehensive database of outcomes, the study seeks to demonstrate the efficacy and safety of the DaVinci SP system, providing insights that could inform clinical practices and enhance surgical techniques in robotic-assisted laparoscopic surgery.

The purpose of this early feasibility study is to evaluate whether the Da Vinci SP system provides adequate visualization, workspace access, instrument reach, and procedural control to safely perform robotic median arcuate ligament release. The study is not powered to demonstrate superiority over existing surgical approaches.
interventions: Single Port Robotic Median Arcuate Ligament Release
title: Novel Feasibility Study Demonstrating the Utility of the Intuitive Da Vinci Single Port Robotic System for Treatment of Median Arcuate Ligament Release

brief_summary: This is an NIH Stage IB single-arm feasibility study will adapt and test the Inpatient Hospice Transitions Checklist (I-HTC), an Epic-embedded intervention supporting hospice eligibility assessment and clinician-surrogate communication for hospitalized persons living with dementia.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of the I-HTC Checklist EHR Intervention (Reported by Clinicians)
title: Inpatient Hospice Transitions Checklist
