title: Changes in the Etiology of Acute Limb Ischemia in the DOAK Era

brief_summary: This retrospective observational study will use historical electronic health record and tinnitus specialty database data from adult patients with tinnitus seen at the Eye and ENT Hospital of Fudan University between January 2015 and August 2026. The study will identify multidimensional tinnitus phenotypes, examine relationships between subjective tinnitus severity and objective audiometric measures, explore within-phenotype heterogeneity, and assess longitudinal phenotype stability and outcome patterns using existing follow-up records. No intervention or additional examination will be performed.
lead_sponsor: Eye & ENT Hospital of Fudan University
title: Multidimensional Phenotyping of Patients With Tinnitus Using Electronic Health Records and a Specialty Database

brief_summary:
This prospective, multicenter study aims to optimize the Magnetocardiography (MCG) algorithm for detecting myocardial ischemia in patients with coronary artery stenosis.

Eligible patients will undergo MCG measurements at rest and following treadmill exercise stress testing. Adenosine pharmacological stress testing may also be performed at the investigator's discretion.

The results of this study will provide clinical data for improving the diagnostic accuracy of MCG in patients with suspected coronary artery disease.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Performance of the MCG-S Algorithm (AUROC)
title: MCG Algorithm Optimization Study in Patients With Coronary Artery Stenosis

brief_summary: STAR-VACC is a randomized double-blind controlled Phase 2 study assessing clinical efficacy of IDH1-vac in patients with newly diagnosed IDH1-mutant high-grade astrocytomas. Over a period of three years, patients with astrocytoma, WHO grade 3-4, will receive up to 12 vaccinations with either IDH1-vac or IS-vac. Screening will be performed after completion of radiotherapy. In the primary treatment phase consisting of 8 vaccinations, patients will receive concurrently SOC temozolomide (up to 12 cycles). Vaccinations will start approx. 4 to 8 weeks after completion of SOC radiotherapy.
title: IDH1-vac in Patients With Newly Diagnosed IDH1R132H-positive High-grade Astrocytomas

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center, observational study aims to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of serum pro-adrenomedullin (Pro-ADM) in adult patients with acute appendicitis and compare its diagnostic performance with conventional inflammatory biomarkers, particularly C-reactive protein (CRP) and the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR).

Acute appendicitis is a common surgical emergency. However, its diagnosis can be challenging because symptoms and laboratory findings are often nonspecific. Although CRP, white blood cell count, and NLR are widely used in clinical practice, their diagnostic accuracy may be limited. Pro-ADM is a biomarker associated with inflammation and infection and may provide additional diagnostic information.

The study will prospectively enroll 400 adult participants at Bursa Yuksek Ihtisas Training and Research Hospital, Turkiye. The study population will include patients undergoing appendectomy for acute appendicitis and a control group of individuals without abdominal pain or active inflammatory disease.

Demographic characteristics, clinical findings, imaging results, and routine laboratory parameters will be recorded. Blood samples will be collected to determine serum Pro-ADM levels.

The diagnostic performance of Pro-ADM will be evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis and compared with conventional inflammatory biomarkers. The study will also investigate the potential value of Pro-ADM in predicting complicated acute appendicitis.

The findings may help clarify whether Pro-ADM could serve as an additional biomarker in the diagnostic evaluation of acute appendicitis.
lead_sponsor: Bursa Yuksek Ihtisas Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy of Serum Pro-Adrenomedullin for Acute Appendicitis
title: Prospective Comparison of Pro-Adrenomedullin, C-Reactive Protein, and Neutrophil-to-Lymphocyte Ratio for Diagnosing Acute Appendicitis

brief_summary: This study will evaluate whether providing ophthalmologists with additional artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted health risk information derived from routine retinal images affects subsequent clinical care in adults attending general ophthalmology clinics. Participating ophthalmologists will be assigned to either usual ophthalmic care or usual ophthalmic care with access to supplementary information generated by an AI system. The AI system does not independently diagnose disease or determine treatment. All clinical decisions remain the responsibility of the ophthalmologist. Participants will receive routine ophthalmic care and will be followed after the ophthalmology visit to collect information on subsequent medical evaluation, newly identified systemic conditions, and changes in clinical management.
lead_sponsor: Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Sun Yat-sen University
primary_outcomes: New systemic diagnosis or clinical management
title: AI-Assisted Systemic Health Risk Assessment in General Ophthalmology: A Cluster Randomized Trial

brief_summary: This single arm double baseline study explored the efficacy and feasibility of the PARTNER program (30h HABIT-ILE + 10h home program) on the functional changes and families' resources of 14 children with unilateral CP aged 24 to 71 months.
title: Effects and Feasibility of a HABIT-ILE and a Home Program on the Bimanual Performance of Children With Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary: The main objective of this study is to validate, in French, new questionnaires assessing disability, quality of life, and patient-reported outcomes in systemic sclerosis.
title: A Clinical Study on Systemic Sclerosis and the Validation of French-language Questionnaires Assessing Disability, Quality of Life, and Disease Status.

brief_summary:
Lymphedema is a chronic condition characterized by the accumulation of lymphatic fluid in tissues, frequently resulting from oncological treatments, trauma, or cancer. This condition causes significant functional impairment and severely impacts patients' quality of life, requiring complex and multidisciplinary therapeutic approaches.

In recent years, reconstructive microsurgery has played an increasingly important role in lymphedema treatment due to high-precision technologies. The use of ultra-high magnification operating microscopes allows the visualization of sub-millimetric vascular structures, enabling lymphatic-venous anastomoses and lymph node transfers on extremely small vessels (0.3-0.5 mm). Additionally, advanced intraoperative imaging, such as indocyanine green fluorescence, allows real-time identification of lymphatic vessels and patency assessment, improving surgical accuracy and clinical outcomes.

While recent experience shows high procedural success rates, a retrospective and systematic analysis of clinical data is necessary to structuredly evaluate functional outcomes. Therefore, this retrospective study aims to analyze the clinical experience gained to define the role of advanced microsurgical technologies in optimizing the therapeutic pathway for patients with lymphedema
interventions: Surgery with and without the aid of Indocyanine Green (ICG)
title: Use of Reconstructive Microsurgery for the Treatment of Lymphedema

brief_summary:
The goal of this retrospective observational study is to evaluate the effectiveness of switching from injectable semaglutide to tirzepatide in adults living with type 2 diabetes (T2D) and, descriptively, in a smaller cohort of adults living with obesity without diabetes, using clinical data from the LMC Diabetes Registry.

The study has two co-primary objectives: 1) to assess change in body weight from baseline to follow-up (6-12 months) among adults living with T2D who switched from injectable semaglutide to tirzepatide, and 2) to assess change in body weight over the same period among adults living with obesity without diabetes who switched.

Secondary objectives will compare changes in body mass index (BMI), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR), waist circumference, blood pressure, alanine transaminase (ALT), lipids, and insulin use from baseline to follow-up between adults living with T2D who switched to tirzepatide and a propensity score-matched group of adults living with T2D who continued semaglutide.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Body Weight at 12 Months - T2D Switch TZP Cohort
Change from Baseline in Body Weight at 12 Months - Obesity Switch TZP Cohort
title: Metabolic Effects of Switching From Injectable Semaglutide to Tirzepatide

brief_summary: This randomized controlled educational trial will compare Directed Self-Learning (DSL) with Instructor-Led Teaching (ILT) for teaching Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) to undergraduate Allied Health Sciences students. Participants will be randomly allocated in a 1:1 ratio to either independently engage with a standardized IPC instructional module or receive faculty-led teaching using the identical module. Knowledge will be assessed using a 20-item multiple-choice questionnaire before and after the intervention. The primary outcome will be knowledge gain, calculated as the difference between post-test and pre-test knowledge scores.
primary_outcomes: Knowledge Gain in Infection Prevention and Control
title: Effectiveness of Directed Self Learning Versus Instructor-Led Teaching Using an Identical Standardized Instructional Module on Infection Prevention and Control Among Undergraduate Allied Health Sciences Students

brief_summary: A multicomponent implementation strategy bundle designed to improve Diabetes Self-Management Education and Support (DSMES) referral and utilization in rural primary care clinics. The initial bundle includes: (1) establishing electronic health record (EHR) referral systems, (2) creating patient face sheets for providers, (3) discussing DSMES referrals during clinician and staff implementation team meetings, and (4) developing DSMES-specific marketing materials and promotional activities.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of Eligible Patients Referred to DSMES
title: Scaling up the DSMES Learning Collaborative

brief_summary: The goal of this randomised controlled trial is to determine the long term safety and tolerability of nano-tocotrienols (50 - 400 mg/day for 6-months duration) to be used as a health supplement in both healthy individuals and those with Type 2 diabetes mellitus. The study will compare patients (both healthy and individuals with Type 2 diabetes mellitus) receiving placebo and those receiving nano-tocotrienols. They would then be followed up at 3 months and 6 months intervals to determine if there is any adverse events experienced with the supplement.
primary_outcomes: Number of events where safety biomarkers fall out of clinically acceptable ranges
title: Tolerability and Safety of Nano-Tocotrienols

brief_summary: The primary goal of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of an integrated therapeutic model - combining VR and standard psychotherapy in improving executive function and hyperarousal adults impacted with mTBI. Specifically, the study will: Evaluate PTSD Symptom Reduction - PTSD symptoms, specifically hyperarousal and hypervigilance will be assessed using the Davidson Trauma Scale, which will provide insight into improvements PTSD symptom reduction.
conditions: Traumatic Brain Injury and Co-occurring Disorders
primary_outcomes: Change in PTSD Symptom Severity Measured by the Davidson Trauma Scale (DTS)
title: Rehabilitation Through Virtual Immersion & Integrated Exposure for Mild Traumatic Brain Injury (ReVIVE for mTBI)

brief_summary:
This clinical trial aims to investigate whether remote ischemic conditioning (RIC) can reduce the risk of cerebral ischemic events, delay clinical progression, and improve long-term outcomes in patients with symptomatic Moyamoya disease (Moyamoya syndrome). The primary research questions include:

Does RIC lower the incidence of cerebral ischemic events (e.g., stroke, transient ischemic attack) compared to standard care? Does RIC slow disease progression, as measured by neuroimaging markers (e.g., cerebral blood flow, collateral vessel development) and clinical assessments? Does RIC improve long-term functional outcomes (e.g., modified Rankin Scale, quality of life) in this patient population? Study Design This is a multicenter, prospective, double-blind, randomized controlled trial (RCT). Eligible participants who provide informed consent and complete baseline evaluations will be dynamically randomized (1:1) via a central randomization system using the minimization method to either the intervention group or the control group.

Intervention Group: Patients will receive RIC therapy (using an automated device) in addition to optimal medical treatment (OMT). RIC will be administered twice daily for 6 months, with each session consisting of 5 cycles of bilateral upper-limb cuff inflation (5 min at a preset high pressure) followed by deflation (5 min), totaling \~45 min per session. OMT includes antiplatelet agents, antihypertensives, antidiabetics, and lipid-lowering drugs as clinically indicated.

Control Group: Patients will receive a sham RIC procedure (using the same device but with cuffs inflated to a fixed low pressure of 60 mmHg) alongside identical OMT. The frequency, duration, and cycling protocol will match those of the intervention group.
primary_outcomes: Ischemic cerebrovascular events within 180 days after intervention
title: A Multicenter, Prospective, Double-blind, Randomized Controlled Study on the Efficacy and Safety of Ischemic Preconditioning Therapy Versus Optimal Medical Therapy in Reducing the Recurrence of Ischemic Events in Symptomatic Moyamoya Disease

brief_summary: This study is being done to find out whether the combination of glofitamab, gemcitabine and oxaliplatin (GemOx) works and is safe in people whose lymphoma has come back or has not responded to previous treatment and has spread to the central nervous system (the brain, spinal cord, cerebrospinal fluid and/or eye). Central nervous system lymphoma is difficult to treat, and there is no agreed standard treatment once it returns. Glofitamab is a bispecific antibody that helps the body's own immune T cells attach to and destroy lymphoma B cells.All participants will receive the study treatment every 3 weeks for up to 6 treatment cycles, followed by maintenance treatment in participants whose lymphoma shrinks or disappears. The main goal is to measure how many participants respond to the treatment; the study will also measure how long responses last and what side effects occur.
lead_sponsor: The First Affiliated Hospital with Nanjing Medical University
title: Glofitamab Plus Gemcitabine and Oxaliplatin (GemOx) in Relapsed or Refractory Primary and Secondary Central Nervous System Lymphoma

brief_summary: Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) is widely underdiagnosed in low- and middle-income countries and regions, due to the lack of accessible tools. Conventional spiromery tests for COPD diagnosis are expensive, require trained personnel to operate properly. Portable spirometry highly relies on the quality assurance of the tests. Since artificial intelligence (AI)-based cough analysis has demonstrated promising results in COPD diagnosis, this study aimed to evaluate the accuracy of an AI-based cough analysis software (Cough Search) compared to a portable spirometer for the auxiliary diagnosis of COPD.
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of LH-002 for COPD diagnosis
Paired differences in sensitivity and specificity between LH-002 and portable spirometry for COPD diagnosis
title: A Prospective, Multicenter, Portable Pulmonary Function Comparison Study Aimed at Evaluating the External Clinical Validation of the Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Auxiliary Diagnostic Software LH-002 (Version: 2.0.0) in Clinical Diagnosis Accuracy

brief_summary: The purpose of this randomized controlled trial is to evaluate the effectiveness of the Vision Care system in preventing falls among hospitalized patients. The study will compare the incidence of falls among patients receiving usual care with that among patients monitored using the Vision Care system during hospitalization.
lead_sponsor: Fundació Institut de Recerca de l'Hospital de la Santa Creu i Sant Pau
title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of Vision Care in Preventing Falls in Hospitalized Patients

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase II clinical trial evaluating the efficacy and safety of FXR0906 in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia or hypertriglyceridemia with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (diagnosed or at increased risk).
conditions: HTG With ASCVD (Diagnosed or at Increased Risk)
lead_sponsor: Fosun Pharmaceutical Industrial Development (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: percent change from baseline at week 24 in fasting triglycerides(TG)
title: A Phase II Study of FXR0906 in Patients With Severe Hypertriglyceridemia or Hypertriglyceridemia With ASCVD.

brief_summary: This randomized pilot study will compare standard hospital discharge communication with discharge summaries simplified using ContextCare, an artificial intelligence-assisted application. The study will enroll 50 adults discharged from Scarborough Health Network. Participants will be assigned to one of two groups in a 1:1 ratio, with allocation stratified by baseline health literacy. The main measure is how well participants explain their diagnosis, treatment, follow-up care, and instructions for seeking further help immediately after receiving discharge information. The study will also assess satisfaction, recall after discharge, and selected post-discharge outcomes.
primary_outcomes: Patient comprehension of discharge instructions: total teach-back score
title: AI-Simplified Discharge Summaries to Improve Patient Comprehension (ContextCare)

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical study is to evaluate the soothing, moisturizing and skin barrier repair effects of two test products by measuring changes in multiple indicators before and after product use, including clinical assessment, non-invasive instrumental measurement, image analysis, lactic acid stinging test and participant self-assessment. It will also explore the residual effect after 2 weeks of discontinuation (only for Serum 2.0). The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Do the two test products provide soothing, moisturizing and skin barrier repair benefits after 4 weeks of continuous use?
* Can Serum 2.0 sustain its efficacy at 1 week and 2 weeks after stopping application?

This is a single-center clinical efficacy study with a 2-week washout period. Approximately 124 healthy Chinese female participants aged 20-40 years will be enrolled and randomly allocated into 2 groups, with around 62 participants in each group. At least 40 participants per group will complete the clinical testing part, and 60 participants per group will complete the questionnaire part.

Researchers will compare skin parameters at multiple time points: baseline (T0), immediately after use (Timm), 1 day after use (T1d), 1 week after use (T1w), 4 weeks after use (T4w), 1 week after discontinuation (T5w, Group A only), and 2 weeks after discontinuation (T6w, Group A only).

Participants will:

* Apply the allocated test product on the full face continuously for 4 weeks
* Attend scheduled on-site visits to receive clinical assessment, instrumental measurement, image analysis, lactic acid stinging test and fill in questionnaires
* Conduct skin status self-assessment at each visit
conditions: Assessment of Soothing, Moisturizing and Skin Barrier Repair Efficacy of Facial Skincare Products in Healthy Women
title: B5 Serum 4-week Clinical Study

brief_summary:
Phase 1, single-center, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial.

Participants (N = 15) will receive a 2-dose schedule (1 vaccination on day 1 and day 28) randomized, receiving either MVA-BN-EBV (n = 12) or placebo (n = 3).
primary_outcomes: Number of participants with Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
Number of participants with a grade 3 or higher AEs assessed as related to trial vaccine
Number of participants with any solicited local and/or systemic AEs for an 8 day period
Number of participants with any postvaccination MAAEs
Number of participants with any postvaccination AESI
title: Phase 1 Trial to Evaluate Safety and Immunogenicity of MVA-BN-EBV in Healthy Young Adults

brief_summary: This prospective, observational patient registry will enroll approximately 1,000 individuals with a clinical or molecular diagnosis of Peutz-Jeghers syndrome (PJS) at participating hospitals in China. The registry will collect standardized clinical information, existing genetic test reports, family history, and longitudinal outcomes. The primary objective is to estimate the 10-year cumulative incidence of a first invasive malignancy after enrollment among participants without a previous malignancy or an unresolved suspected malignancy at baseline, accounting for death as a competing event. Secondary objectives address organ-specific malignancies, new primary cancers in participants with a cancer history, mortality, major polyp-related complications, and clinical and STK11 variant characteristics. Participants may be followed for up to 20 years. Biospecimen donation, additional baseline sampling, research sequencing, and patient-derived organoid studies are optional and require the corresponding consent. Refusal of an optional component does not preclude participation in the clinical registry. No treatment or clinical surveillance strategy is assigned by the study.
primary_outcomes: 10-year cumulative incidence of a first invasive malignancy
title: Chinese Multicenter Registry for Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome

brief_summary:
The TRANSITION-CGM trial will evaluate whether starting continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) before hospital discharge improves blood glucose control in adults with type 2 diabetes compared with usual care using finger-stick blood glucose checks. The study focuses on the transition from hospital to home, when patients may face changes in diabetes medications and challenges managing their blood glucose levels.

This single-center, randomized controlled trial will enroll approximately 218 adults with type 2 diabetes, a hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) 9% and above, and treatment with insulin and/or oral diabetes medications. Participants will be recruited during hospitalization and must be expected to return home after discharge. People already using a CGM will not be eligible.

Participants will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to one of two groups. The CGM group will start using a continuous glucose monitor before discharge and receive device training and written instructions. The usual-care group will continue finger-stick blood glucose monitoring and receive standard discharge education. Both groups will receive assistance with outpatient diabetes follow-up. Diabetes medications will be managed by treating clinicians according to usual clinical practice.

Participants will be followed for approximately 12 weeks after discharge, with an early follow-up encounter and a final assessment at 12 weeks. The primary outcome is HbA1c at 12 weeks, a blood test that reflects average blood glucose levels over approximately three months. Secondary outcomes include diabetes-related hospitalizations and episodes of low blood sugar. Additional exploratory measures include CGM use, follow-up attendance, patient-reported experiences, and time spent within the target glucose range when CGM data are available.

The study will determine whether initiating CGM during hospitalization can improve glycemic control after discharge and provide preliminary evidence about its effects on diabetes-related hospitalizations and hypoglycemia.
primary_outcomes: Glycemic control as measured by Hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c)
title: Transitioning Recently Admitted Patients With Non-Insulin and Insulin-treated Type 2 Diabetes to Innovative Glucose Monitoring

brief_summary: This prospective observational study will examine how electrosurgical activation patterns during elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy are associated with surgeon experience and intraoperative difficulty. Adult patients scheduled for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy at University Hospital of Split will receive standard clinical care; the study does not assign an intervention or change the surgical technique. A fixed camera will record only the laparoscopic monitor, and a directional microphone will record the audible signals of the electrosurgical generator. The study includes a cross-sectional comparison among surgeons with different cumulative experience and a longitudinal assessment of developing surgeons as they gain additional experience. Activation patterns will be analyzed separately during dissection of the hepatocystic triangle and separation of the gallbladder from the liver bed. Intraoperative difficulty will be graded from the initial operative video using the Parkland Grading Scale by two independent assessors, with adjudication when needed.
primary_outcomes: Median Duration of Coagulation-Mode Electrosurgical Activations During Segment A
Longitudinal Change in Median Coagulation Activation Duration During Segment A
title: Electrosurgical Patterns and Learning Curve in Elective Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn about the effectiveness and safety of aztreonam-avibactam, an antibiotic used to treat infections caused by highly resistant bacteria, in adults with weakened immune systems.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

How well does aztreonam-avibactam work in treating these infections?

How many participants recover, and how many die or develop another infection caused by the same bacteria?

What side effects or medical problems occur during or after treatment?

Researchers will also compare participants treated with aztreonam-avibactam with a group of participants previously treated with ceftazidime-avibactam plus aztreonam. This comparison will help researchers understand differences in treatment outcomes.

The study will include adults with weakened immune systems, such as people with cancer, organ transplants, or those receiving medicines that suppress the immune system.

Participants will:

Receive antibiotic treatment chosen by their treating physicians as part of routine medical care.

Have their medical records reviewed to collect information about their infections, treatments, and outcomes.

Be followed for up to 60 days after starting treatment to assess recovery, survival, side effects, and recurrence of infection.

Researchers will not assign treatments or change participants' medical care.
lead_sponsor: Centro de Educación Medica e Investigaciones Clínicas Norberto Quirno
title: Aztreonam-Avibactam in Immunocompromised Hosts

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to learn whether a computer-based support tool called DEXI (Dermoscopy EXplainable Intelligence) can help dermatologists decide whether a lesion may be melanoma, a serious type of skin cancer. DEXI uses artificial intelligence, or AI, which means computer technology that looks for patterns in images and information. DEXI works within a software program called the DermaGraphix Visualizer, which displays and organizes skin and lesion images. The goal of this study is to see whether DEXI can help doctors find melanoma and reduce biopsies that may not be needed.
conditions: Other and Unspecified Malignant Neoplasm of Skin
Neoplasm of Uncertain Behavior of Skin
Neoplasm of Unspecified Behavior of Bone, Soft Tissue, and Skin
Skin Changes Due to Chronic Exposure to Nonionizing Radiation
primary_outcomes: Overall melanoma detection rate per visit
title: Using an Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tool for Melanoma Diagnosis

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated the effectiveness of a telerehabilitation-based exercise program in individuals who had undergone surgery for lumbar disc herniation. Participants were assigned to a control group, a home exercise group, or a telerehabilitation group. The exercise programs started four weeks after surgery and continued for eight weeks, three days per week, with each session lasting 30-45 minutes. The home exercise group performed the exercise program independently at home, while the telerehabilitation group performed the same program under remote supervision of a physiotherapist using video calls. The control group continued their routine daily activities without participating in a structured exercise program during the study period. Pain, disability, physical activity, and health-related quality of life were assessed before and after the eight-week intervention period.
primary_outcomes: Change in Functional Disability Assessed by the Oswestry Disability Index (ODI)
Pain Intensity Assessed by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS)
Physical Activity Assessed by the International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ)
Health-Related Quality of Life Assessed by the 36-Item Short Form Health Survey (SF-36)
title: Telerehabilitation After Lumbar Disc Herniation Surgery

brief_summary: This single-center, randomized, parallel-group trial evaluates whether adding a structured psychological and organizational support module to the standard technical debriefing via the PEARLS method after a full-scale hospital mass-casualty incident simulation increases healthcare professionals' confidence in their institution's ability to respond to a mass-casualty incident. Adult hospital professionals with an operational role in the exercise will complete a baseline questionnaire immediately after the exercise and before allocation. Participants will then be randomized 1:1 to standard debriefing control module or to standard debriefing plus a structured psychological and organizational support module. The primary outcome is the post-debriefing institutional confidence score, calculated as the mean of three 7-point Likert items and analyzed with adjustment for the pre-debriefing score.
title: Structured Debriefing and Institutional Trust After a Mass-Casualty Simulation

brief_summary:
This study evaluates the safety, efficacy, and health economic outcomes of modular robotic-assisted minimally invasive esophagectomy (RAMIE) compared with conventional thoracoscopic minimally invasive esophagectomy (MIE) in patients with resectable esophageal cancer.

Participants are randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo either modular robotic-assisted esophagectomy using the Carina™ Surgical Platform (experimental group) or conventional thoracoscopic esophagectomy (control group). The primary endpoint is the rate of Textbook Outcome (TO) within 30 days post-operation. Secondary endpoints include operative parameters, quality of life, overall survival, disease-free survival, and health economic metrics.
title: Modular Robot-Assisted Versus Conventional Minimally Invasive Esophagectomy for Esophageal Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn more about how doctors can create a complete electrical block in the heart during catheter ablation procedures used to treat certain abnormal heart rhythms. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How often do electrical signals continue to travel through a blood vessel around the heart after ablation?
* Which ablation applications are most important for achieving a successful electrical block?
* How do different procedural factors affect the success of the treatment?

Participants who undergo a catheter ablation procedure as part of their normal medical care may take part in this study. No additional tests, visits, or procedures will be required. Researchers will collect information that is routinely recorded during the procedure to better understand how electrical signals travel in the heart and how ablation procedures can be improved.
primary_outcomes: Anatomical Zone of the Effective Coronary Sinus RF Application
RF Power of the Effective Coronary Sinus RF Application
Duration of the Effective Coronary Sinus RF Application
Contact Force of the Effective Coronary Sinus RF Application
Ablation Index of the Effective Coronary Sinus RF Application
Cumulative Epicardial RF Time to Mitral Isthmus Block
Relative Order of the Effective Coronary Sinus RF Application
title: Conduction Breakthrough in the Coronary Sinus Post Endocardial Mitral Isthmus Ablation

brief_summary: This study will examine the associations of respiratory muscle strength and trunk muscle mechanical properties with dynamic balance and limits of stability in healthy young adults. The research will enroll healthy volunteers between the ages of 18 and 30. Participants will undergo assessments to measure their maximal inspiratory and expiratory pressures, as well as the tone and stiffness of their abdominal and lumbar paraspinal muscles. Additionally, the participants will complete computerized balance tests to evaluate their voluntary weight-shifting capabilities and their stability on a moving surface. Ultimately, the findings will determine whether evaluating these respiratory and trunk muscle characteristics will effectively complement standard clinical balance assessments.
interventions: Myotonometry, Respiratory Muscle Strength Testing, and Computerized Balance Assessment
primary_outcomes: Score of The Limits of Stability
Score of The Dynamic Bipedal Balance Test
title: Associations of Respiratory Muscle Strength and Trunk Muscle Mechanical Properties With Dynamic Postural Control

brief_summary:
This study looked at whether regular follow-up by pharmacists through phone calls (telepharmacy) can help improve the treatment of anaemia in patients undergoing haemodialysis.

Anaemia is very common in patients with kidney disease and can cause fatigue, weakness, and an increased risk of heart problems. It is usually treated with medications such as erythropoietin (EPO), but managing the correct dose and ensuring patients follow treatment can be challenging. In this study, patients were divided into two groups. One group received standard care, while the other group received additional support from pharmacists through regular phone calls. During these calls, pharmacists helped patients understand their medications, encouraged adherence, monitored symptoms, and worked with doctors to adjust treatment when needed.
title: Impact of Telepharmacy on Hemodialysis Outcomes

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to compare two devices, PAL device manufactured by Microaire Surgical Instruments, LLC and the Harmonic Vibrator liposuction device to see if there is a difference in the outcome of the procedure with either device. The PAL device will be used on one side of the body and the investigational Harmonic Vibrator device on the other side of the body.
title: A Prospective Randomized Study to Evaluate the Benefits of Harmonic Vibration Liposuction

brief_summary: This study evaluates the reliability of CT-based assessment of acromial morphology and its relationship with age, in order to improve understanding of shoulder pathologies such as subacromial impingement and rotator cuff tears.
primary_outcomes: Intra-Rater and Inter-Rater Reliability of the Bigliani Classification of Acromial Morphology
title: Acromial Morphology: Reliability of CT-based Assessment and Relationship With Age in a Series of 420 Patients

brief_summary:
Human papilloma virus (HPV) is the most common viral infection of the reproductive system and is spread through contact with infected genital skin, mucous membranes, or bodily fluids. This study will assess an experimental vaccine called 10 valent Human Papillomavirus Virus (10vHPV) for the safety, reactivity, and immune response, in healthy adults, compared to Gardasil 9.

There are two phases in this study - Phase 1 will include up to 36 healthy adults aged 18-25 years, Phase 2 will include 36 healthy adults aged 26-45 years. Participants will be randomised in a 2-to-1 ratio to receive either 10vHPV or Gardasil 9.

10vHPV or Gardasil 9 will be administered as a 0.5 mL single dose via intramuscular injection in the deltoid muscle of the upper arm. In Phase 1, participants will receive a single dose on Day 1, and in Phase 2, participants will receive a single dose on Day 1, 2 months, and 6 months.
lead_sponsor: Serum Institute of India Pvt. Ltd.
primary_outcomes: To assess the safety and reactogenicity of a single dose of 10vHPV vaccine in comparison with a single dose of Gardasil 9 vaccine in healthy adults aged 18 to 25 years in phase 1.

To assess the safety of 3 doses (administered at day 0, 60 and 180) of 10vHPV vaccine in comparison with 3 doses (administered at day 0, 60 and 180) of Gardasil 9 vaccine in healthy adults aged 26 to 45 years.
title: Clinical Trial to Assess the Safety, Tolerability, Reactogenicity, and Immunogenicity of a 10 Valent Human Papillomavirus Virus (10vHPV) Vaccine

brief_summary: Further decompensation (FD) in cirrhosis represents a prognostic stage associated with an even higher mortality than that associated with the first decompensation. The Baveno VII conference defined FD as a second portal hypertension (PH)-driven decompensating event (ascites, VB, or hepatic encephalopathy) and/or jaundice, or development of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and/or hepatorenal syndrome-acute kidney injury HRS-AKI. This randomized controlled trial aims to evaluate the effect of TIPS versus standard of care on survival without further decompensation during a 24-month follow up period in patients with cirrhosis after a first PH-related decompensation.
title: "Anticipant"-TIPS After a First Portal-hypertension-related Complication in Cirrhosis

brief_summary: This will be a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-centre study with the aim to establish metabolic improvements in individuals diagnosed with hyperuricemia associated with gout by treatment with CMA2 including N-acetyl-L-cysteine (NAC), L-carnitine-L-tartrate (LCAT), nicotinamide (niacinamide), and L-serine for 4 weeks.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the effect of 4-weeks administration of CMA2 treatment on serum uric acid levels in participants diagnosed with hyperuricemia associated with gout, as compared with placebo.
title: Combined Metabolic Activator Supplementation in Subjects Diagnosed With Gout

brief_summary:
Background: Chronic non-nociceptive or nociplastic pain and neurological sequelae following stroke are associated with substantial functional impairment and reduced quality of life. Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is a non-invasive neuromodulation technique capable of modulating cortical excitability and functional brain networks involved in pain processing and neurological recovery. However, its clinical response may vary according to the underlying phenotype and therapeutic target.

Objective: To evaluate the safety, tolerability, and clinical response to rTMS as a complementary therapeutic intervention in patients with chronic non-nociceptive pain, fibromyalgia, myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome (ME/CFS), Long COVID, and post-stroke sequelae, and to explore differences in treatment response across clinical conditions.

Methods: A clinical study including baseline assessment, rTMS intervention, post-treatment evaluation, and follow-up was conducted. The protocol consisted of ten treatment sessions administered over two consecutive weeks. For chronic pain, fibromyalgia, ME/CFS, and Long COVID, excitatory stimulation at 10 Hz was delivered over the left primary motor cortex (M1), with 1,000 pulses per session. For post-stroke sequelae, inhibitory stimulation at 1 Hz with 600 pulses was applied according to the predominant clinical deficit. Target localization was performed using neuronavigation when individual magnetic resonance imaging was available and the international 10-20 system when it was not. Clinical outcomes included pain, fatigue, sleep, quality of life, motor function, and language performance, assessed using validated clinical scales.
title: Transcraneal Magnetic Stimulation for Treatment of Non-nociceptive Pain in Chronic Diseases

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to test whether circadian-informed bedtime recommendations can improve sleep, next-day psychomotor vigilance, and subjective well-being among healthy adults. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Can Optimal Bedtime derived from data collected by a consumer smartwatch increase the objective total sleep time?
* Can Optimal Bedtime derived from data collected by a consumer smartwatch reduce the count of lapse in a next-day Psychomotor Vigilance Task?
* Can Optimal Bedtime derived from data collected by a consumer smartwatch increase subjective sleep quality?

Researchers will compare Optimal Bedtime with a placebo bedtime and an unguided baseline in a cross-over design.

Participants will:

* Be randomized 1:1 to either Optimal Bedtime then placebo or placebo then Optimal Bedtime.
* Wear a consumer smartwatch for 6 weeks, 2 weeks in each of baseline, Optimal Bedtime, and placebo.
* Complete a Psychomotor Vigilance Task and a subjective well-being survey every morning.
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline and Placebo in Total Sleep Time
Change from Baseline and Placebo in the Count of Lapse in Psychomotor Vigilance Task (PVT)
Change from Baseline and Placebo in Subjective Sleep Quality
title: Circadian-informed Optimal Bedtime

brief_summary:
This study will look at the health characteristics of adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in Kazakhstan. Researchers want to better understand how this liver condition appears in people in Kazakhstan and how it is managed in everyday medical care.

About 420 adults with MASLD will take part. Researchers will collect information from their medical records, laboratory tests, liver imaging, and questionnaires.

A smaller group of about 65 participants in Almaty who were already prescribed Ursosan® by their doctor before joining the study will be followed for 6 months. Researchers will look at changes in a liver enzyme called alanine aminotransferase (ALT) and other measures of liver health. The study does not assign Ursosan® or any other treatment. Treatment decisions are made by each participant's doctor as part of their usual medical care.

The results may help researchers better understand MASLD in Kazakhstan and how people with MASLD respond to Ursosan® when it is used in everyday medical care.
lead_sponsor: Kazakh Association of Internal Medicine Specialists
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With Hepatic Steatosis According to Imaging
Proportion of Participants With Liver Fibrosis According to FibroScan
Proportion of Participants With Liver Cirrhosis According to FibroScan
Proportion of Participants With at Least 30% Reduction in ALT From Baseline
title: Clinical Profile of Patients With MASLD in Kazakhstan and Clinical Effectiveness of Ursosan in Almaty

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the effects of visual rehabilitation and vestibular rehabilitation added to conventional physiotherapy on postural stability, pain, and functional status in individuals with knee osteoarthritis. Participants will be randomly assigned to three groups: conventional physiotherapy, conventional physiotherapy combined with visual rehabilitation, or conventional physiotherapy combined with vestibular rehabilitation. The study will evaluate changes in balance, pain, and functional performance before and after the intervention.
title: Effects of Visual and Vestibular Rehabilitation in Individuals With Knee Osteoarthritis

brief_summary: Previous research has demonstrated that itch and pain share several underlying neural pathways and signaling molecules. Understanding these common mechanisms is important for developing more effective therapeutic strategies targeting both sensations. Mepyramine, an antihistamine, has been reported to exert effects on both itch and pain perception. In this study, we aim to investigate these effects using established experimental models of itch and pain. Itch will be induced using histamine, a naturally occurring substance in the human body, and spicules from the plant Mucuna pruriens (cowhage), while electrical stimulation will be used to assess pain-related responses. By combining these experimental approaches, we aim to better understand how mepyramine influences different sensory mechanisms. The overall purpose of this study is to evaluate the effects of mepyramine on experimentally induced itch and pain in healthy volunteers.
primary_outcomes: Measuring itch by computerized Visual Analog Scale Scoring
title: Pain Sensitivity and Pruritus of Peripheral Nerves

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 2 trial enrolling approximately 150 pre-menopausal women with bacterial vaginosis (BV). Participants will be randomized 1:1:1 to three groups. All participants will receive oral metronidazole 0.4 g twice daily for 7 days. In addition, participants will take vaginal capsules (high-dose WST03, low-dose WST03, or matched placebo) once daily for 14 days. The primary endpoint is cumulative BV recurrence rate at Week 12. This trial evaluates the efficacy and safety of WST03 plus metronidazole for lowering BV recurrence and explores its impact on vaginal microecology.
lead_sponsor: SPH Sine Pharmaceutical Laboratories Co., Ltd.
primary_outcomes: Cumulative recurrence rate of bacterial vaginosis (BV) up to Week-12 visit
title: WST03 Capsule Combined With Metronidazole for Bacterial Vaginosis

brief_summary: This study is being done to answer the following question: Can adding a treatment called Fecal Microbiota Transplant (FMT) to the usual treatment delay the growth or spread of cancer better than the usual treatment alone? FMT treatment changes the bacteria in the gut called the microbiome.
primary_outcomes: Progression Free Survival based on RECIST 1.1 criteria
title: Immune Checkpoint Blockade and Chemotherapy With or Without Fecal Microbiota Transplant in Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

brief_summary: This study aims to develop and validate the Learning to Communicate Successfully Approach (LCSA), a culturally sensitive communication intervention manual for Urdu-speaking adults with chronic aphasia. Aphasia is a language disorder that can affect speaking, understanding, reading, writing, and everyday communication, commonly following stroke or other neurological conditions. The LCSA addresses communication difficulties while also considering participation in daily life, communication partners, the communication environment, and personal and psychosocial factors. The study evaluates the feasibility, applicability, and outcomes of the LCSA approach in Urdu-speaking adults with chronic aphasia.
title: Learning to Communicate Successfully Approach for Urdu Speaking Patients With Chronic Aphasia

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to see if the Empower-ICE\_Fit program can help people with dementia live more safely, comfortably, and independently at home. This program is designed to better match a person's physical and mental abilities (intrinsic capacity) with their living space (environment) through targeted home environmental assessment and home modification counseling.

As a multiphase mixed-methods study, researchers will collect both numerical health data and personal interview feedback to fully understand how the program works.

The main questions this study aims to answer are:

Does the Empower-ICE\_Fit program improve the daily functional performance of people with dementia?

Does this empowerment-based approach help improve the quality of life for both the individuals and their family caregivers?

In this study, researchers will:

Assess the current home environments and daily functioning of the participants using specific home environment screening measures.

Provide tailored home modification recommendations with empowerment-based approach.

Compare the health and safety outcomes of participants in the Empower-ICE\_Fit program with those receiving standard care.

Conduct interviews to deeply understand the personal experiences and challenges of participants and their caregivers during the process.

Participants will be asked to complete regular health assessments (including both professionally guided and self-reported measures) and may be invited to share their care experiences in interviews.
primary_outcomes: Change in Social Engagement and Independence (EID-Q-C)
title: The Effects of an Empower_ICE-Fit Program in PLwD Living at Home

brief_summary:
Inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD), including Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis, are chronic inflammatory conditions of the digestive tract that frequently lead to malnutrition. Malnutrition in individuals with IBD is associated with diminished quality of life, impaired treatment response, and higher rates of hospital admission. To standardize nutritional diagnosis, the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) introduced a consensus framework combining phenotypic criteria (weight loss, low body mass index, and reduced muscle mass) and etiologic criteria (reduced food intake/assimilation and disease-related inflammation).

The primary objective of this prospective observational study is to validate the diagnostic accuracy and sensitivity of the GLIM criteria in identifying malnutrition among hospitalized and ambulatory adult patients with IBD, using the Subjective Global Assessment (SGA) as the reference standard. Secondary objectives include determining the prevalence and severity of GLIM-defined malnutrition, evaluating its relationship with clinical, functional, and inflammatory parameters, and identifying clinical predictors of malnutrition in this population.

Adult participants diagnosed with IBD presenting to the inpatient wards or outpatient clinics of Al-Rajhi Liver Hospital (Assiut University) will be enrolled. Participants will undergo initial nutritional risk screening using the Malnutrition Universal Screening Tool (MUST) for outpatients or the Nutritional Risk Screening 2002 (NRS-2002) for inpatients. Full nutritional assessment will be conducted via GLIM criteria and SGA. Additional evaluations will include anthropometric measurements (mid-arm muscle circumference and calf circumference), muscle strength testing via handgrip dynamometry, dietary intake assessment, routine laboratory panels (complete blood count, inflammatory markers, liver function tests, electrolytes, and fecal calprotectin), and endoscopic disease activity scores (SES-CD or Mayo endoscopic score) when clinically available.
primary_outcomes: Diagnostic Accuracy and Sensitivity of the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) Criteria
title: Validation and Clinical Impact of GLIM Criteria in Patients With Inflammatory Bowel Disease

title: Study of Cross-Cutting E-Health Prevention Approaches

brief_summary:
The goal of this interventional study is to evaluate the efficacy and perception a commercial LED device in 110 healthy adult females and males between the ages of 35-65 years old, inclusively. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does daily use of this commercial LED device improve overall skin appearance as measured by clinical tools (expert clinical grading, cutometer, digital photography, and VISIA-CR? Does daily use of this commercial LED device improve subjective skin appearance? Is daily use of this commercial LED device well tolerated?

Participants will complete a 9-minute LED treatment (4.5 minutes LED, 4.5 minutes LED+ infrared light therapy) with a commercially available device every day for 12 weeks. They will visit the clinic three times (baseline, 6 weeks, 12 weeks) for clinical grading of skin.
primary_outcomes: Subjective and objective tolerance to device use
title: Efficacy of an LED Mask

brief_summary: This randomized, double-blind, active placebo-controlled superiority trial will evaluate whether intravenous esketamine reduces time to psychiatric hospital discharge in adults hospitalized because of acute suicide risk. A total of 106 participants will be randomized in a 1:1 ratio to receive intravenous esketamine or midazolam as an active placebo. Participants assigned to esketamine will receive eight 40-minute intravenous infusions at a dose of 0.5 mg/kg administered twice weekly. The primary outcome is time from the first study infusion to psychiatric hospital discharge. Secondary outcomes include suicidal ideation and behavior, depressive symptoms, psychological pain, hopelessness, global clinical improvement, safety, tolerability, dissociative symptoms, and healthcare costs. Exploratory analyses will investigate peripheral inflammatory markers, BDNF, and polygenic risk scores as potential predictors or mediators of treatment response. Clinical follow-up will continue through Week 12.
title: Intravenous Ketamine for Acute Suicidal Crisis and Psychiatric Hospital Length of Stay

brief_summary: This study is a prospective, single-arm, multicenter, exploratory clinical trial. It aims to evaluate the efficacy and safety of chidamide combined with benmelstobart, nab-paclitaxel, and immunogenic radiotherapy (SBRT) as second-line treatment in patients with advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC). The study plans to enroll 41 BTC patients who have previously received first-line systemic therapy, and these patients will receive chidamide, benmelstobart, nab-paclitaxel, and SBRT. The primary endpoint is progression-free survival (PFS), and the secondary endpoints include objective response rate (ORR), duration of response (DoR), overall survival (OS), and safety.
lead_sponsor: The Affiliated Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital of Nanjing University Medical School
title: Chidamide Combined With Benmelstobart, Nab-paclitaxel, and SBRT as Second-Line Treatment for Advanced BTC

brief_summary:
Glycemic responses vary significantly among individuals, even when consuming identical foods or meals, but the factors predicting individual glucose responses to food intake remain poorly investigated. The aim of the LIfestyle MEtabotype (LIME) study is to identify lifestyle-related and mechanistic factors which predict individual postprandial glucose fluctuations in individuals with different glycemic status (prediabetes, type 2 diabetes \[T2D\] and absence of prediabetes or T2D), using comprehensive lifestyle characterization and metabolic, molecular and neurocognitive phenotyping.

As part of this phenotyping, the LIME study also investigates the role of ketone bodies. Individuals with insulin resistance, prediabetes or T2D often show impaired cerebral glucose utilization. Ketone bodies, such as β-hydroxybutyrate (βHB) may serve as an alternative energy source for the brain. However, how exogenous βHB affects neurocognitive processes and decision-making in individuals with different glycemic status remains poorly understood.

This record describes module B of the LIME study. Module B investigates the effects of a single dose of exogenous βHB, compared with a carbohydrate-based placebo drink, on brain structure and function, decision-making behavior and physiological and metabolic responses. Module A comprises a comprehensive lifestyle and metabolic characterization of the same participants and is registered separately as an observational study (NCT07868601). Data from both modules will be integrated in joint analyses.
primary_outcomes: βHB response to exogenous βHB supplementation
Fasting and postprandial glucose and insulin response
Heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV)
title: LIfestyle MEtabotype Study B (LIME-B)

brief_summary: Malignant tumors of the biliary system are highly invasive and malignant with an increasing incidence rate. Comprehensive drug therapy is the main treatment for advanced biliary tract tumors, yet the current gemcitabine plus platinum-based chemotherapy regimens yield suboptimal efficacy maintenance in patients with advanced biliary tract tumors. There is an urgent need for effective second-line treatment regimens for advanced biliary tract tumors. Vicinecumab is a recombinant humanized anti-EGFR monoclonal antibody generated by conjugating a potent cytotoxic small molecule to trastuzumab. It inhibits tumor cell proliferation and promotes tumor cell death by blocking various cellular physiological functions including mitosis. Current research data have demonstrated that in patients with recurrent and metastatic nasopharyngeal carcinoma who have received systemic therapy, vicinecumab can significantly improve patients' survival and prognosis compared with the chemotherapy group, with a manageable safety profile. Therefore, this study aims to observe and evaluate the efficacy and safety of vicinecumab in the second-line and subsequent treatment of advanced biliary tract tumors.
title: Single-arm, Multicenter, Open-label Phase II Study of Vedotin for Injection in Second-line or Later Treatment of Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer

brief_summary: This study evaluates whether applying RECELL® autologous skin cell suspension (ASCS) to one half of a split-thickness skin graft (STSG) donor site accelerates re-epithelialization and improves long-term scar quality compared with the untreated half of the same donor site. Using a prospective, randomized, intra-patient (split-site) controlled design, each participant's donor site is divided into two contiguous, comparable halves at the time of surgery; one half is randomized to receive RECELL® application plus standard transparent film dressing, while the other receives standard dressing alone. Each participant serves as their own control, eliminating inter-patient variability in healing. Participants are followed for 12 months with serial standardized digital photography, blinded outcome assessment, and validated scar-assessment instruments (POSAS 2.0, Vancouver Scar Scale).
title: Autologous Skin Cell Suspension (RECELL®) for Accelerated Healing of Split-Thickness Skin Graft Donor Sites: A Randomized, Intra-Patient (Split-Site) Controlled Trial

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the feasibility of using artificial intelligence (AI)-generated clinical decision support during routine inpatient hospital medicine care. Participating hospitalist physicians may receive AI-generated recommendations for eligible hospitalized patients under their care. Eligible patient cases will be randomly assigned to one of three AI prompting strategies that differ in the clinical information provided to the AI system. After reviewing each recommendation, participating physicians will complete a brief survey assessing the clinical usefulness of the recommendation, how they interpreted it, and whether it was or will be incorporated into patient management.

The study will assess whether AI-generated recommendations can be successfully generated and delivered during routine clinical care and whether physicians complete the study surveys and adopt the recommendations. It will also provide preliminary information about physicians' perceptions of AI-generated recommendations across the three prompting strategies. The findings will be used to inform the design of a future larger randomized trial of AI-initiated clinical decision support.
interventions: AI Clinical Decision Support: Automated EHR Data Retrieval
AI Clinical Decision Support: Admission H&P Note
title: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-Initiated Clinical Decision Support in Hospitalist Practice

brief_summary: Carbon fiber custom dynamic orthoses (CDOs) include a full-length footplate, a stiff posterior spring, and a cuff that wraps around the leg below the knee. CDOs restore function after limb trauma, decrease forefoot loading, and reduce pain. However, initial introduction to a CDO is not consistent, so this study is being conducted to determine if different methods of training alter forefoot loading during gait. Unimpaired adult participants will be randomized to one of three groups: 1) no feedback, 2) visual feedback of forefoot force, and 3) visual feedback of cuff forces. All participants will walk at a controlled speed on a treadmill without the CDO, after initial introduction to the CDO, and after completing two rounds of training in the CDO.
title: Comparative Effect of Training Methods to Reduce Forefoot Loading in Carbon Fiber Custom Dynamic Orthoses

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effects of a single session of manual acupuncture on oxidative stress and state anxiety in active smokers. Oxidative stress will be assessed using plasma malondialdehyde (MDA), while state anxiety will be evaluated using the State Anxiety Inventory (SAI). Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either manual acupuncture or sham acupuncture. MDA concentration and SAI scores will be assessed at baseline and 90 minutes after completion of the intervention. The study will also explore the correlation between changes in plasma MDA concentration and changes in SAI scores to assess the relationship between oxidative stress and state anxiety following the intervention.
title: Effects of Manual Acupuncture on Malondialdehyde Levels and State Anxiety Inventory Scores in Active Smokers: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to evaluate the effects of connective tissue massage (CTM) added to electromyographic biofeedback (EMG-BF) in adults with dyssynergic defecation (DD). The study will assess bowel function, constipation severity, anal sphincter function, quality of life, and anxiety.

The study will include adults aged 18 years and older who have functional constipation according to the Rome IV criteria and a physician-confirmed diagnosis of DD.

Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups:

Control group: Participants will receive patient education and EMG-BF. Treatment group: Participants will receive the same patient education and EMG-BF, with additional CTM.

Both groups will receive 12 treatment sessions over 6 weeks, with two sessions per week. Patient education will cover pelvic floor muscle anatomy, defecation physiology, diaphragmatic breathing, correct defecation posture and straining, nutrition, fluid intake, and physical activity.

Researchers will assess participants before and after treatment. Assessments will include a 7-day bowel diary, constipation severity, anal sphincter activity measured by surface electromyography, constipation-related quality of life, and anxiety. Researchers will also record participants' physical, demographic, and clinical characteristics.
title: Effects of Connective Tissue Massage Plus Biofeedback for Dyssynergic Defecation

brief_summary:
Subtle changes in language are among the early signs of cognitive decline in Alzheimer's disease and related conditions. Researchers are therefore studying whether language can help identify cognitive changes earlier and at larger scale. Conversational AI tools (large language models, or LLMs) such as ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude are now widely used, including by middle-aged and older adults. A conversation with an AI chatbot is more than a sample of written language: it shows how a person works toward a goal over several exchanges. This includes how they phrase requests, add constraints, keep track of context, notice errors, and revise their instructions. These behaviors may reflect language, attention, working memory, planning, and other aspects of cognitive function.

This exploratory, observational study will examine whether features of people's conversations with AI chatbots are associated with performance on a standard cognitive screening test. The study does not involve any treatment or intervention and is not intended to diagnose Alzheimer's disease, mild cognitive impairment, dementia, or any other condition.

Participants: 100 adults aged 60 and above who use AI chatbots and are proficient in English. Participants are recruited online through research crowdsourcing platforms (Prolific and DataForce). They do not need to have, or report, any diagnosis. No participants are recruited through clinics or hospitals.

Procedure: Participants complete a single online session of about 20 to 30 minutes. After giving informed consent, they:

Complete a background questionnaire covering demographics, language background, and AI chatbot use. Optional questions cover relevant medical and family history.

Upload three to five of their own previous conversations with an AI chatbot. They are asked to remove names and other identifying details first and to avoid highly sensitive conversations. They then answer a few short questions about each conversation.

Complete two short everyday tasks with a chatbot in the study interface: planning an activity and drafting a short message. The timing of typing and messages within the study interface is recorded.

Complete a remote MoCA test (XpressO), a validated self-administered digital cognitive screening tool, and the PHQ-8, a brief questionnaire on depressive symptoms.

A subset of participants may be invited to an optional additional assessment: the standard Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), administered by a trained examiner over video call. This is used to check how well the online test agrees with standard administration, and requires separate consent.

Outcomes: The primary outcome is the association between linguistic and interactional features of participants' AI conversations and their cognitive screening score, analyzed mainly as a continuous measure. Features include how specific and well structured requests are, how context is maintained, repetition, clarification, error recognition, revision strategies, progress through multi-step tasks, and typing and timing patterns. Secondary aims are to describe how adults aged 60 and over use AI chatbots, and to assess whether these features could support future computational methods for studying early cognitive change. Demographic, language, health, mood, and technology-use variables are considered as possible confounders.

Risks and safeguards: The study is minimal risk. The main risk is to privacy, because past chatbot conversations may contain personal information. Participants choose which conversations to share and are asked to remove identifying details. The research team removes any remaining direct identifiers, and data are stored on secure, access-restricted university servers. Data are analyzed by the academic research team and its research partner for research purposes only. Participants may feel mild fatigue or frustration; they can skip questions, take breaks, or stop at any time, and receive proportional compensation if they stop early. Individual scores are not reported. Participants whose screening score falls in the range that may indicate impairment receive a non-diagnostic note that explains the limits of screening tests and suggests discussing any memory concerns with a physician.
primary_outcomes: Association between features of human-AI chatbot conversations and cognitive screening score
title: Human-LLM Conversations as a Digital Signature of Cognitive Performance in Adults

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate the accuracy and safety of the RIGHTEST iFree 2 Continuous Glucose Monitoring (CGM) System in pregnant women with type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, or gestational diabetes. The system uses a small sensor placed under the skin to measure glucose levels in the fluid between cells.

Approximately 104 women will participate at study sites in Germany and Taiwan. Each participant will wear two sensors, one on each upper arm, for up to 15 days. During one clinic visit lasting up to six hours, blood samples will be collected every 15 minutes. Sensor readings will be compared with laboratory blood glucose measurements to assess accuracy.

Participants will also be assessed for side effects, including skin reactions at the sensor sites, and will receive a safety follow-up after sensor removal. No procedures will be used to deliberately raise or lower blood glucose levels.
interventions: RIGHTEST iFree 2 Continuous Glucose Monitoring System
primary_outcomes: Percentage of CGM Readings Within ±20% of Reference Blood Glucose Measurements
title: RIGHTEST iFree 2 CGM in Pregnant Women With Diabetes Study

brief_summary:
This study aimed to evaluate the effects of using a stress ball during femoral catheter removal on quality of recovery, patient comfort, and pain in adults undergoing coronary angiography.

The study was conducted at a hospital in Istanbul, Türkiye, between November 2024 and May 2025. A total of 84 patients participated in this randomized controlled trial. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups, with 42 patients in each group.

Patients in the intervention group were asked to repeatedly squeeze and release a stress ball during femoral catheter removal. Patients in the control group received routine clinical care without the stress ball intervention.

Pain was assessed 15 minutes after catheter removal. Quality of recovery and patient comfort were evaluated before discharge using standardized assessment scales.

The study was designed to determine whether stress ball use could improve recovery and comfort and reduce pain during care following coronary angiography.
title: Effects of Stress Ball Use During Femoral Catheter Removal After Coronary Angiography
