brief_summary:
This study aimed to compare the dentoalveolar, skeletal, dental arch, transverse, and soft tissue effects of maxillary molar distalization performed with the Power Bar appliance using different mandibular anchorage methods, and to evaluate the additional effects of low-level laser therapy on orthodontic tooth movement.

A total of 57 participants were evaluated in four groups according to the anchorage approach used during treatment: miniscrew anchorage (n=14), orthodontic button anchorage (n=14), lingual arch anchorage (n=14), and a control group (n=15). In the three active treatment groups, maxillary molar distalization was performed using the Power Bar appliance. The treatment groups differed primarily according to the mandibular anchorage method used to support the distalization mechanics.

Low-level laser therapy was also evaluated within the active treatment groups using a split-mouth design. One side received low-level laser therapy, while the contralateral side did not receive laser application and served as an intra-individual comparison side. This design allowed the potential effect of laser therapy to be evaluated while reducing inter-individual variability.

Clinical and orthodontic records obtained before treatment (T0) and after the distalization period (T1) were compared. Skeletal, dentoalveolar, dental, dental arch, transverse, and soft tissue changes were assessed to determine the effects of the different anchorage methods and to investigate whether low-level laser therapy provided an additional effect during Power Bar-assisted maxillary molar distalization.
primary_outcomes: Change in Maxillary First Molar Distalization
title: Effects of Different Anchorage Methods and Low-Level Laser Therapy in Power Bar Distalization

brief_summary:
Caffeine is commonly used by athletes to improve performance, but not everyone responds to it in the same way. In weight-class sports like wrestling, athletes are grouped by body weight. When caffeine is dosed based on body weight (4 mg per kg), heavier athletes receive a larger total amount of caffeine than lighter athletes. This study asked whether the effects of caffeine on wrestling performance and side effects differ across wrestling weight classes.

Ninety-five male wrestlers (30 lightweight, 36 middleweight, and 29 heavyweight) completed two testing sessions: one after taking caffeine (4 mg/kg) and one after taking a placebo (an inactive capsule). Neither the wrestlers nor the researchers knew which capsule was given in each session. Each session included a countermovement jump test and a wrestling-specific fitness test that involved throwing a wrestling dummy. Heart rate, perceived exertion, and self-reported symptoms were also recorded.

The study found that lightweight and middleweight wrestlers generally performed better after caffeine, while heavyweight wrestlers showed no performance improvement and reported more side effects, such as anxiety, rapid heartbeat, stomach discomfort, and insomnia. These differences occurred even though all wrestlers received the same caffeine dose relative to their body weight.

The results suggest that a standard body-weight-based caffeine dose may not work equally well for all wrestlers. Lighter wrestlers may benefit more, while heavier wrestlers may experience more side effects without performance gains. These findings support the need for individualized caffeine dosing strategies in wrestling and similar weight-class sports. However, because body weight, total caffeine dose, and other weight-class-related factors were not separated in this study, the results should be considered exploratory and do not establish weight-specific recommendations.
title: Caffeine and Wrestling Performance in Male Wrestlers of Different Weight Classes: A Randomized Crossover Trial

brief_summary: This study aims to develop and validate multimodal AI-based prediction models for peripheral intravenous catheter (PIVC)-related phlebitis by integrating demographic, clinical, catheter-related, and phlebitis image data. The models will be evaluated for their ability to accurately predict phlebitis risk, with the goal of facilitating early identification, timely intervention, and improved patient safety.
primary_outcomes: Performance of the AI-Based Prediction Model
title: AI Prediction of PIVC-Related Phlebitis

brief_summary:
Thoracic hyperkyphosis is a postural disorder characterized by excessive thoracic curvature exceeding 40°, which may negatively affect proprioception, postural alignment, and muscle mechanical properties. Kinesiology taping (KT) has been proposed as a non-invasive intervention to improve postural control and proprioceptive feedback through cutaneous mechanoreceptor stimulation. However, evidence regarding its immediate effects on thoracic proprioception and muscle mechanical properties in young adults with thoracic hyperkyphosis remains limited.

This sham-controlled randomized clinical trial aims to investigate the immediate effects of kinesiology taping on thoracic joint position sense, postural alignment, and muscle mechanical properties in young adults with thoracic hyperkyphosis. Muscle tone, stiffness, and elasticity will be assessed using MyotonPRO, alongside measurements of thoracic proprioception and postural alignment.

The study will compare kinesiology taping with sham taping to determine whether kinesiology taping produces greater immediate improvements in these outcomes. The findings are expected to provide further evidence regarding the short-term sensorimotor and biomechanical effects of kinesiology taping in individuals with thoracic hyperkyphosis.
title: Kinesio Taping in Young Adults With Thoracic Hyperkyphosis

brief_summary: his real-world observational study examines whether sensation-seeking personality traits influence the clinical response to transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) in patients with treatment-resistant depression (TRD). Participants will complete a validated sensation seeking scale prior to TMS treatment, and depressive symptoms will be assessed using standardized clinical scales during and after the TMS course.
primary_outcomes: Correlation Between Change in Montgomery-Åsberg Depression Rating Scale (MADRS) Scores and Baseline Sensation Seeking Scale (SSS) Total Score
title: Sensation Seeking and TMS Response in TRD

brief_summary: Although exercise and physical activity have shown beneficial effects in individuals with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), evidence regarding the effects of daily physical activity habits on sleep quality and respiratory parameters remains limited. This study aims to investigate these associations in individuals with OSA.
title: Physical Activity, Sleep Quality, and Respiratory Function in Obstructive Sleep Apnea

brief_summary: This pilot feasibility study used a randomized, double-blind, within-subject crossover design to explore temporal interference (TI) stimulation in adults with major depressive disorder. Fifteen participants received five weekly 20-minute stimulation sessions in randomized order, including TI stimulation targeting the left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, left subgenual anterior cingulate cortex, right amygdala, and right ventral striatum, as well as a sham stimulation condition. The primary aim was to establish the feasibility of target-specific TI stimulation and to characterize its effects on functional connectivity and cognitive-emotional processing, assessed by resting-state fMRI and an emotional Stroop task before and after each session. Depressive and anxiety symptoms (HAMD and HAMA) were collected longitudinally across the five-week protocol as a secondary, exploratory measure.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants Who Completed All Five Stimulation Sessions
Number of Participants With Adverse Events
title: Temporal Interference Stimulation in Major Depressive Disorder: A Pilot Feasibility Study

brief_summary: This phase II/III trial compares the usual treatment (daratumumab and hyaluronidase, lenalidomide, bortezomib and dexamethasone \[DaraRVd\] regimen followed by autologous stem cell transplant \[ASCT\] followed by maintenance therapy) to DaraRVd treatment followed by bispecific antibody therapy (teclistamab and/or talquetamab) followed by maintenance therapy in treating patients with newly diagnosed, standard risk multiple myeloma. Daratumumab is in a class of medications called monoclonal antibodies. Daratumumab and hyaluronidase works by helping the body to slow or stop the growth of cancer cells. Hyaluronidase is an endoglycosidase. It helps to keep daratumumab in the body longer so that the medication will have a greater effect. Lenalidomide is in a class of medications called immunomodulatory agents. It works by helping the bone marrow to produce normal blood cells and by killing abnormal cells in the bone marrow. Bortezomib blocks several molecular pathways in a cell and may cause cancer cells to die. It is a type of proteasome inhibitor and a type of dipeptidyl boronic acid. Dexamethasone is in a class of medications called corticosteroids. It is used to reduce inflammation and lower the body's immune response to help lessen the side effects of chemotherapy drugs. Teclistamab and talquetamab are bispecific monoclonal antibodies that can bind to targets on both cancer cells and immune cells (T-cells) that may help the body's immune system attack the cancer, and may interfere with the ability of cancer cells to grow and spread. Giving DaraRVd followed by teclistamab and/or talquetamab may work better in increasing the likelihood of reducing the cancer burden to the point that it is undetectable, and prolonging the time until the cancer returns compared to DaraRVd followed by ASCT.
lead_sponsor: Alliance for Clinical Trials in Oncology
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients who are classified as being MRD-negative post-consolidation (Phase II)
title: Comparing Bispecific Antibody Treatment to Autologous Stem Cell Transplant for Newly Diagnosed, Standard Risk Multiple Myeloma

brief_summary:
The COMFORT study will evaluate an artificial intelligence-based platform developed to support the clinical assessment of kidney and prostate cancer. The platform utilises imaging data to provide AI-generated outputs intended to assist clinicians in the assessment of suspected lesions.

The primary objective of the study is to assess the role of the COMFORT platform in the clinical decision making process of clinicians managing kidney or prostate cancer cases.

Secondary objectives include evaluation of the performance of AI models on anatomical segmentations, tumor characterisation (localisation, volumetric measurements, lesion classification, and scoring (e.g., Bosniak, PI-RADS, RENAL). Also the acceptability, usability, utility and trustworthiness of the AI models will be evaluated.

In addition, potential causes of privacy leakage associated with the COMFORT AI models will be evaluated as part of the platform's privacy assessment.

brief_summary: This study will evaluate whether adding G-CSF to standard treatment improves outcomes in newborns (0-28 days) with sepsis and neutropenia. It will compare survival, recovery of neutrophil counts, hospital stay, infections, and adverse effects between babies receiving G-CSF and standard treatment alone.
title: G-CSF In Neonatal Sepsis With Neutropenia

brief_summary:
Since 2019, the International Rescue Committee (IRC) has led family planning programming under the Women's Integrated Sexual Health (WISH) program, funded by the United Kingdom's Foreign, Commonwealth, and Development Office. This study will assess contraceptive-related outcomes in communities in South Sudan where the IRC is implementing a standard set of family planning services.

Approximately one year into their standard implementation, the IRC will develop additional interventions to augment the standard, which this study will evaluate over the subsequent three years. This additive intervention will aim to optimize last-mile service delivery by increasing access to self-managed family planning methods, such as oral contraceptive pills, emergency contraception, and self-injectable contraception.

This study's evaluations are independent from the IRC and is one of four studies in the Guttmacher Institute's Family Planning Impact Lab (FPIL). FPIL intends to produce experimental research, estimating the causal impact of various family planning interventions on women's broader health, wellbeing, and development outcomes in South Sudan, Somalia, Chad, and Sierra Leone.
primary_outcomes: Change in the proportion and number of women reporting use of self-managed contraceptive methods (self-administered injectable, OCPs, emergency contraception, condoms, fertility-awareness based methods) between baseline, midline, and endline
Change in the proportion and number of women using preference-aligned fertility management between baseline, midline, and endline
Change in the proportion and number of women using contraceptive methods (including modern or any) between baseline, midline, and endline
title: Estimating the Impact of Comprehensive SRHR Services on Health and Development in South Sudan for the Family Planning Impact Lab

brief_summary:
The trial is expected to enroll 50 confirmed cases of type 1 or type 2 diabetes. All eligible subjects must wear a continuous glucose monitoring system on both the left and right upper arms for a maximum of 15 days (360 hours) and adhere to the clinical visit protocol.

After enrollment, all subjects will be randomly assigned to either Group A or Group B to determine the time points for clinical visits. All subjects will have venous blood drawn on days 1, days 5 (±1), 10 (±1), and 15 (-1) post-wearing. All subjects will remove all devices on day 15 (-1) based on system prompts and undergo a telephone follow-up on day 4 (±3) thereafter. This clinical trial does not involve long-term follow-up.

During the trial, the blood glucose values measured by the "continuous glucose monitoring system" worn by the subjects will be analyzed against the YSI venous blood glucose values measured at the medical institution on days 1, 5 (±1), 10 (±1), and 15 (-1) as control reference values. This analysis aims to evaluate the accuracy, repeatability, stability, high and low blood glucose event alerts, and safety of the continuous glucose monitoring system.

Additionally, fingertip blood glucose measurements taken by subjects during home use will be collected to assess the operational feasibility of the continuous glucose monitoring system in a home setting.
title: Effectiveness and Safety of the RIGHTEST™ CGM System for Blood Glucose Management in Persons With Diabetes Mellitus

brief_summary:
In this study, researchers will learn more about the use of felzartamab in participants with immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN). IgAN is a kidney disease caused by the buildup of an antibody called IgA in the kidneys over time. In people with IgAN, abnormal IgA and other antibodies form clusters that build up in the small filters of the kidneys, which leads to inflammation and damage. Felzartamab is designed to target certain immune cells that produce these abnormal antibodies.

The main goal of the study is to learn about the effect felzartamab has on the buildup of IgA clusters in the kidneys. The main question that researchers want to answer is:

• How much does the buildup of IgA in the kidney change from the start of the study to Week 36? Researchers will also learn about the effect felzartamab has on kidney health by measuring protein levels in the urine and the kidneys' ability to filter blood. They will also learn more about the safety of felzartamab and how the body processes the drug.

The study will be done as follows:

* Participants will be screened to check if they can join the study.
* This is an open-label study, which means both the researchers and the participants will know that all participants are receiving felzartamab.
* Participants will receive felzartamab as intravenous (IV) infusions.
* Participants will have kidney biopsies done over the course of the study to help measure changes in the health of the kidneys.
* Participants will have multiple scheduled study visits over about 104 weeks. An extra study visit may be needed if a participant decides to leave the study early.
* In total, participants will stay in the study for about 2 years (up to 112 weeks).
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Mesangial Immunoglobulin A (IgA) Deposition by Immunofluorescence (IF)
title: A Study to Learn About the Effects of Felzartamab on the Kidneys of Adults With Immunoglobulin A Nephropathy (IgAN)

brief_summary:
This study aims to explore the experiences of mothers who are currently breastfeeding their children but are considering stopping breastfeeding. It focuses on how mothers make decisions about breastfeeding cessation, where they seek information about possible methods, what uncertainties or difficulties they experience, and what support they need from healthcare professionals.

This is a qualitative study using a phenomenological approach. Approximately 20 to 25 mothers aged 18 years or older who are currently breastfeeding a child aged at least 6 months and are considering breastfeeding cessation will be invited to participate. The final number of participants will depend on the information obtained during the interviews.

Data will be collected through individual, semi-structured interviews lasting approximately 30 to 45 minutes. Participants will also complete a brief form about their demographic characteristics and breastfeeding experiences. Interviews will be conducted face-to-face or online, depending on participant preference.

The findings are expected to provide a better understanding of mothers' experiences and support needs during the breastfeeding cessation decision-making process and may help inform breastfeeding counseling provided by healthcare professionals.
primary_outcomes: Experiences of Mothers Considering Breastfeeding Cessation
title: Experiences of Mothers Considering Breastfeeding Cessation: Decision-Making, Method Exploration, and Support Needs

brief_summary:
Spinal Muscular Atrophy (SMA) is a disease that causes progressive muscle weakness. There are many types- the most severe and most common, type 1, affects very young babies, and is life-threatening if untreated. Other types can cause significant disability. Most cases are caused by a missing part of the survival motor neuron 1 (SMN1) gene. Another related gene, SMN2, can partially compensate for this affected gene. With more copies of SMN2 broadly leading to a milder disease.

Three new treatments can slow or prevent symptoms, but they work best when given before symptoms appear. This has led to many countries, including the USA and much of Europe, introducing newborn screening (NBS) for SMA, so that affected babies can be treated as early as possible. The investigators ran a UK pilot project that screened nearly 33,000 babies and found the test to be accurate and practical, but this pilot was too small to show whether screening improves outcomes or is good value for money for the NHS. The UK National Screening Committee would also like to know how acceptable NBS for SMA is for different groups of people. This study is designed to answer those questions.

Screening will be introduced across seven NHS screening laboratories, most of which already screen for another rare condition, severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID). About 400,000 babies are born in the areas covered by these laboratories every year. Screening will be introduced gradually, so that the investigators can compare babies born before and after screening starts, with screening between the autumn of 2026 and autumn 2027.

This will be followed by a period of only SMA NBS which will continue until autumn 2030. This will be compared to a period of no screening from autumn 2024 until autumn 2027 to include babies born before any laboratory starts screening and where the screening laboratories have not yet opened during the study.

The study has two phases:

Phase 1 will examine how successfully SMA NBS can be delivered through the NHS, and will look at:

* Whether screening can accurately identify SMA
* How quickly screening results are returned
* Whether babies diagnosed through SMA NBS start treatment earlier than those diagnosed because of symptoms
* How many parent(s)/guardian(s)/guardians agree to take part in screening
* How different groups feel about SMA NBS and whether there are any areas of the process that need to be improved

Phase 2 will examine whether SMA NBS improves children's lives and will look at:

* Longer-term health outcomes, including whether treated children with SMA diagnosed by NBS or standard of care (SoC) can walk independently by 24 months
* Quality of life for children and families with SMA diagnosed by NBS or SoC
* Evaluate overall costs and benefits for the NHS

How will the study work?

* It will be led by the University of Oxford, with input from hospitals, laboratories, patient groups, and experts across the UK.
* Parent(s)/guardian(s) will be asked for consent when their baby has the routine heel-prick blood test. No extra blood will be needed.
* A national clinical network called SMA REACH, will provide information about the milestones babies reach and their general health.
* All other information will be asked for directly from parent(s)/guardian(s) with children who have SMA
* Health economists will use information collected to update an existing mathematical model on cost-effectiveness. This will estimate whether the benefits of early diagnosis and treatment outweigh the costs of screening.

The study will give the UK National Screening Committee (UK NSC) clear, high-quality evidence on whether newborn screening for SMA is feasible, acceptable, beneficial for children and families, and good value for the NHS.
title: Service Evaluation for Newborn Screening for Spinal Muscular Atrophy

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate if obinutuzumab beta works to treat primary IgA nephropathy with active proliferative lesions in adults. It will also learn about the safety of obinutuzumab beta. The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does obinutuzumab beta reduce 24-hour urinary protein at Week 24 compared with baseline? Does obinutuzumab beta improve kidney function, reduce hematuria, and lower Gd-IgA1 levels? Does obinutuzumab beta change active lesionson repeat kidney biopsy at Week 52? Researchers will also look at B-cell depletion, disease relapse, and the proportion of participants achieving proteinuria \<0.5 g/d.

Participants will:

Receive obinutuzumab beta 1000 mg by intravenous infusion 4 times: at Week 0, Week 2, Week 24, and Week 26.

Continue their usual supportive kidney care (maximum tolerated ACEi or ARB, with or without stable SGLT2i or MRA).

Visit the clinic at Weeks 0, 2, 12, 24, 26, 36, and 52 (8 visits including screening).
primary_outcomes: Percent change in 24-hour urinary protein from baseline at Week 24

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized controlled clinical trial is to learn if adding fruquintinib to short-course radiotherapy, tislelizumab, and CAPOX can improve neoadjuvant treatment response and is safe for adults with locally advanced low rectal cancer. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does adding fruquintinib increase the pathological complete response (pCR) rate after neoadjuvant therapy?
* What adverse events do participants experience when fruquintinib is added to the regimen? Researchers will compare short-course radiotherapy followed by fruquintinib + tislelizumab + CAPOX with short-course radiotherapy followed by tislelizumab + CAPOX to see if adding fruquintinib improves the tumor response to neoadjuvant treatment.

Participants will:

* Receive short-course radiotherapy (e.g., 25 Gy in 5 daily fractions over 1 week)
* Receive either fruquintinib + tislelizumab + CAPOX (experimental arm) or tislelizumab + CAPOX (control arm) for the neoadjuvant cycles
* Attend scheduled visits for tumor assessment (MRI, endoscopy, CT), blood tests, and adverse-event monitoring
* Undergo total mesorectal excision (TME) surgery after neoadjuvant treatment and have the specimen evaluated for pathological response
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants achieving pathological complete response (pCR; ypT0N0)
title: SCRT + Fruquintinib + Tislelizumab + CAPOX Versus SCRT + Tislelizumab + CAPOX as Neoadjuvant Therapy for Locally Advanced Low Rectal Cancer

brief_summary: Patients undergoing heart valve surgery require cardiopulmonary bypass, a procedure that can lead to a temporary reduction in blood flow to major organs and subsequent ischemia-reperfusion injury, thereby triggering postoperative complications such as acute kidney injury and delirium. Current treatments for these complications primarily involve pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions. Pharmacological interventions are not routinely employed due to limited supporting evidence, while non-pharmacological interventions are labor-intensive and lack systemic protective effects; thus, there is an urgent need for a systemic, non-pharmacological intervention that is easy to implement. This study aims to investigate the organ-protective effects of remote ischemic preconditioning-administered at different time points-following heart valve surgery, with the goal of developing a safe, effective, and clinically scalable nursing intervention protocol. Through this research, the investigators hope to further reduce the incidence of postoperative complications and improve clinical outcomes and prognoses for patients undergoing heart valve surgery.
primary_outcomes: the incidence of postoperative acute kidney injury
title: Effects of Remote Ischemic Preconditioning at Different Time Phases in Patients Undergoing Heart Valve Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether temporal interference (TI) stimulation, added to usual clinical treatment, improves symptoms of schizophrenia and is safe and tolerable. Approximately 100 adults aged 18 to 60 years with schizophrenia will be randomly assigned in equal numbers to active TI or sham TI. Participants and researchers assessing treatment outcomes will not know which treatment has been assigned.

Participants will continue usual clinical treatment and receive two 30-minute stimulation sessions daily for 14 consecutive days, for a total of 28 sessions. Symptoms will be assessed before treatment and on Days 7, 15, and 45. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans will be obtained before treatment and on Day 15. Side effects will be monitored throughout participation.

The main question is whether active TI produces a greater improvement in overall schizophrenia symptoms from baseline to Day 15 than sham TI. The study will also assess symptom improvement at other time points, changes in other symptoms, treatment completion, safety, and changes in brain imaging measures.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS) Total Score at Day 15
title: Temporal Interference Stimulation (TI) for Schizophrenia (SCZ)

brief_summary:
Chronic musculoskeletal pain is common in older adults and is associated with reduced mobility, loss of function, poorer quality of life, fear of movement, fear of falling and a higher risk of falls. Exercise programmes are effective in preventing falls, but very few programmes combine fall-prevention exercise with pain self-management, including pain science education, for older people who live in the community and have both chronic pain and an increased risk of falling.

The goal of this pilot randomised controlled feasibility trial is to find out whether it is feasible, acceptable and safe to deliver a 12-week supervised group programme (MovePainFall) that combines multicomponent exercise with pain science and fall-prevention education, compared with a control group that maintains usual activities, in community-dwelling adults aged 65 years or over with chronic musculoskeletal pain (lasting 3 months or more).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is it feasible to recruit, randomise, retain and engage participants (recruitment rate, eligibility, adherence, retention) and is the programme safe and acceptable?
* What are the preliminary effects of the programme on mobility, balance, lower-limb strength, dual-task performance, pain intensity and interference, fear of falling, fear of movement and quality of life?

Researchers will compare the MovePainFall group with the control group to estimate feasibility parameters and preliminary effect sizes that will inform the design and sample size of a future full-scale randomised controlled trial.

Participants in the MovePainFall group will:

* attend three supervised 60-minute group exercise sessions per week for 12 weeks (warm-up, strength and power, challenging balance, motor-cognitive dual-task training, functional gait and daily-living tasks, relaxation);
* attend one additional 30-45-minute group education session per week on pain neuroscience, pain self-management and fall prevention.

Participants in the control group will maintain their usual activities and routine health care and may be invited to attend the programme after the post-intervention assessment (waiting list).

All participants will be assessed by blinded assessors before randomisation and after the 12-week intervention period.
primary_outcomes: Acceptability: Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC)
title: Multicomponent Exercise and Pain Science Education for Fall Prevention in Older Adults With Chronic Musculoskeletal Pain (MovePainFall)

brief_summary:
This multicenter translational research study integrates diagnostic analyses and ex-vivo functional testing to support future clinical trials evaluating the safety and efficacy of CFTR modulator treatments in individuals with cystic fibrosis (CF) carrying rare or orphan mutations that may benefit from these therapies.

Patient-derived nasal epithelial cells will be collected through standardized nasal brushing procedures, expanded, and cultured under air-liquid interface conditions to generate differentiated epithelia. Short-circuit current measurements will be used to assess baseline CFTR dysfunction and evaluate functional recovery following treatment with available CFTR modulators. These results will be complemented by DNA sequencing to identify complex alleles, quantitative and qualitative CFTR mRNA analyses to investigate gene expression and splicing defects, and assessments of epithelial transcriptomics, surface liquid viscosity, and mucociliary transport to identify additional mechanisms contributing to CF-like lung disease.

The study will not include patient follow-up. The duration of participation will be limited to the time required to perform and analyze the nasal brushing procedure. Baseline CFTR activity will be compared with previously published data from individuals without cystic fibrosis.
title: A Precision Medicine Approach to Assess Protein Function Loss and the Potential for CFTR Function Restoration in Cystic Fibrosis and Related Disorders

brief_summary:
Several HoLEP techniques have been developed, with the conventional tri-lobar and the en-bloc approaches being the most commonly practiced. Although both techniques achieve comparable functional outcomes and safety profiles, they differ in surgical dissection strategy and anatomical orientation. Some authors suggest that the en-bloc technique may facilitate maintenance of the correct surgical plane, whereas others consider the tri-lobar approach easier for surgeons familiar with transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP). However, evidence comparing their learning characteristics remains limited.

Most published studies evaluating the HoLEP learning curve have investigated a single surgical technique or assessed a second technique after surgeons had already gained substantial HoLEP experience. Such study designs introduce significant bias because increasing surgical experience inevitably influences subsequent performance.

A prospective alternating design, in which a HoLEP-naïve surgeon performs consecutive tri-lobar and en-bloc procedures, may provide a more balanced comparison by exposing both techniques to similar levels of cumulative surgical experience while minimizing temporal bias.
conditions: Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia With Outflow Obstruction
primary_outcomes: Number of cases required to achieve procedural proficiency
title: Learning Curve of Tri-lobar HoLEP Versus En-bloc HoLEP

brief_summary:
Our team recently pilot tested a new mobile app, PolarUs, co-designed with people who live with bipolar disorder (BD), to support BD self-management and quality of life (QoL) measurement. An initial study suggested the app improved QoL and mood scores over time among participants in Canada and the United States.

This project aims to fully assess whether PolarUs improves QoL and mood outcomes in diverse people with BD living in Canada and the United States. To achieve this, we have (1) culturally and linguistically adapted the English version of PolarUs into French, Mandarin, and Spanish, and (2) are now conducting a randomized controlled trial (RCT) to assess whether PolarUs (in all 4 languages) improves QoL and mood outcomes in adults living with BD in Canada and the United States.

Participants will:

1. Attend an eligibility assessment interview to confirm their eligibility to participate.
2. Eligible participants will be randomly assigned (like flipping a coin) to one of two groups:

   Group 1 - Receive access to the PolarUs app through participants' Android (Google) or iOS (Apple) mobile device for a period of 12 weeks.

   Group 2 - Receive access to the PolarUs app after a 12-week waiting period. During the waiting period, participants will only receive study assessments.
3. Participants will complete study assessments at the beginning and end of the 12-week period and, where appropriate, monthly during the study period.

We aim to recruit approximately 480 participants from Canada and the United States to take part in the study. We would also like to understand how people with bipolar disorder use and engage with the app.
primary_outcomes: Brief Quality of Life in Bipolar Disorder (QoL.BD) Scale
title: Evaluating the PolarUs App in People With Bipolar Disorder

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to evaluate whether local application of a 4% bovine lactoferrin nanohydrogel improves soft tissue healing, bone healing, and implant stability following immediate dental implant placement in mandibular molar sites.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does the use of a Lactoferrin Nano-Hydrogel in combination with healing abutments enhance bone and soft tissue regeneration, reduce peri-implant inflammation, and improve the success rate of immediate implant placement in mandibular molars compared to conventional healing methods?

Researchers will compare immediate implant placement with local application of the 4% bovine lactoferrin nanohydrogel to the same surgical procedure without the nanohydrogel to evaluate differences in bone healing, marginal bone levels, implant stability, soft tissue healing, clinical inflammation, and postoperative pain.
conditions: Immediate Dental Implant Placement Dental Implant Stability Soft Tissue Healing Bone Regeneration Lactoferrin Nanohydrogel
primary_outcomes: Change in Peri-Implant Marginal Bone Level
title: Lactoferrin Nanohydrogel for Soft And Hard Tissue Healing and Implant Stability in Immediate Implant Placement

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the effects of glucose consumption (in the form of Christmas cookies) on platelet function, as well as the motivation and willingness of healthy platelet donors.The main hypothesis is that consuming Christmas cookies before platelet donation can improve platelet function in vitro and increase donor satisfaction.

This is a double-blinded, prospective, crossover interventional study. Participants (regular platelet donors at the department of Transfusion Medicine and Cell Therapy, Medical University of Vienna) must donate twice during the study period, while receiving either one or multiple (up to ten) Christmas cookies.

Before and after each donation, participants will be asked to complete a questionnaire on their satisfaction with platelet donations. Platelet function will be analyzed using a Platelet Function Analyzer (PFA-100) before and after each donation. In selected cases, Light Transmission Aggregometry of Born (LTA) will be used to analyze blood samples from the participants and the platelet concentrate before and after the donation.

The study period will last from November 6, 2026, to December 24, 2026. Participants must be between 18 and 70 years old and should not have any food intolerances or allergies. Furthermore, humorless participants will be excluded using a specifically designed questionnaire.
primary_outcomes: Change in platelet function after consumption of Christmas cookies
Change in happiness after consumption of Christmas cookies
title: Cookies for Platelets

brief_summary:
This study aimed to evaluate whether abdominal massage could reduce abdominal pain, constipation, and gas/bloating in patients receiving enteral nutrition through a nasogastric tube after surgery for head and neck cancer.

A total of 70 patients participated in this randomized controlled trial. Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups. The intervention group (35 patients) received abdominal massage for 15 minutes twice daily over three consecutive postoperative days, in addition to routine nursing care. The control group (35 patients) received routine nursing care without abdominal massage. Abdominal pain, constipation, and gas/bloating were assessed using standardized measurement tools. Assessments were performed twice daily, in the morning and evening, during the first three postoperative days.

The study was conducted to investigate whether abdominal massage could be a useful non-drug nursing intervention for managing gastrointestinal symptoms in patients recovering from head and neck cancer surgery.
title: Effect of Abdominal Massage on Gastrointestinal Symptoms After Head and Neck Cancer Surgery

brief_summary: The aim of the study is to assess health status and quality of life during the post-sepsis period using patient-reported outcome measures. Patients will be classified into two groups according to treatment received during hospitalization for sepsis or septic shock: those who received standard-of-care treatment alone and those who additionally received Efferon® LPS hemoadsorption. The study will compare post-sepsis outcomes between the two groups over a 12-month follow-up period.

brief_summary:
The purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of EB06 intravenous infusion (loading dose of 20mg/kg followed by a maintenance dose of 10mg/kg) compared with placebo in adults with moderate to severe non-segmental vitiligo..

Vitiligo is a chronic autoimmune skin disorder characterized by the loss of skin pigmentation due to the destruction of melanocytes. EB06 is a fully human monoclonal antibody that binds and neutralizes CXCL10, a chemokine implicated in the trafficking of anti-melanocytic T-cells to the epidermis and in inducing cell death. Elevated levels of CXCL10 have been associated with both the initiation of the disease and the maintenance of vitiligo lesions. The study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of EB06 in adults with moderate to severe non-segmental vitiligo.
primary_outcomes: Mean percent change from baseline in F-VASI at Week 28
title: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Study to Evaluate the Safety and Efficacy of EB06 Versus Placebo in Adults With Moderate to Severe Non-segmental Vitiligo

brief_summary:
This clinical trial aims to investigate if oral immunotherapy can help children with egg allergy tolerate eggs.

Children aged 6-18 months can take part in the trial.

Main question: What percentage of children can tolerate eggs after oral immunotherapy, compared with children who avoid eggs?

Children are assigned to these two groups by chance.

Children receiving oral immunotherapy will:

* Take a small, increasing amount of raw egg daily for 1-1.5 years
* Attend clinic or online visits each time the dose is increased
* Record missed doses

All children will:

* Provide blood samples to measure allergy-related markers
* Undergo an oral food challenge with raw egg after 1-1.5 years to assess how much they can tolerate
* Report allergic reactions (parent-reported)
* Complete questionnaires (parent-reported)
* Participate in an end-of-study telephone interview with an allergy nurse (parent-reported)
title: Oral Immunotherapy for Children With Egg Allergy

brief_summary: This study compared an Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) care program with conventional perioperative care in adults undergoing surgery for colorectal cancer. Participants were randomly assigned to receive either ERAS care or usual care. The ERAS program included coordinated measures before, during, and after surgery aimed at supporting faster and safer recovery. The study evaluated whether ERAS could reduce the length of hospital stay and improve postoperative recovery. Other outcomes included early mobilization, return of bowel function and oral feeding, postoperative pain, complications and adverse events, removal of urinary catheters and drains, discontinuation of intravenous therapy, and selected laboratory measures. The study was conducted at the General Anticancer Oncology Hospital of Athens "Saint Savvas" in Greece.
title: Enhanced Recovery After Surgery in Patients Undergoing Colorectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
Multiple sclerosis (MS) as leading cause of non-traumatic neurological disability in young adults has additionally to the individual's burden of disease a significant influence on their ability to work.

Objective of this study is to test parameters for their correlation with weekly working hours.

We will retrospectively analyse data of people with MS (pwMS) and correlate weekly working hours with demographics, Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), Nine Hole Peg Test (9HPT), walking speed measured by Timed 25-Foot Walk test (T25FW), Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) and Hand Grip Strength (HGS).

This study will be closely monitoring a program designed to treat spasticity using an epidural stimulator to better understand its effects on spasticity and voluntary movement.

brief_summary:
We are doing this study to find the best way to manage pain during a procedure called urethral bulking. This procedure treats urine leakage that happens with coughing, laughing, sneezing, or physical activity. It works by injecting a gel-like substance around the urethra (the tube that urine comes out of) to help it stay closed when it should.

We use a numbing gel (called lidocaine jelly) inside the urethra to help with pain during the procedure. In this study, we will also be administering lidocaine (numbing medication) injected around the urethra or a saline placebo (medical grade saltwater) injection, which has no numbing effect. A placebo is something that looks like a real treatment but doesn't have any medical effect. Both the lidocaine and the saline would be injected around the urethra using a small needle, and we'll compare how well they work at reducing pain.
title: This Study is Comparing Pain Outcomes After Urethral Bulking When Participants Are Randomized to Two Different Pain Medication Regimens.

brief_summary: Demonstrating the real-world effectiveness of Isa-VRD in routine NHS care is the key aim for this proposal Isatuximab (Isa) is an IgG1 monoclonal antibody that binds a specific epitope on the human CD38 receptor and has antitumour activity via multiple mechanisms of action. In the Phase 3 multicentre randomised study IMROZ, Isa in combination with velcade, lenalidomide and dexamethasone (VRD) was compared to VRD in transplant-ineligible (TIE) patient with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma (MM). In the UK however, bone marrow (BM)-based MRD testing is not routinely available and poorly utilised in everyday practice. Limited access, the need for repeated invasive procedures, and service capacity constraints hinder widespread, longitudinal BM MRD assessment - particularly for TIE, newly diagnosed MM patients treated outside of specialised centres. As a result, routine monitoring often relies on conventional serum tests (serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation electrophoresis and serum free light chain assays), which lack the analytical sensitivity to consistently detect very low-level disease.
lead_sponsor: The Royal Wolverhampton Hospitals NHS Trust
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients maintaining sustained PRD-negative status
title: REAL World IMROZ OutcomEs (REALIZE Study)

brief_summary: Based on clinical observation data from two previously enrolled cases, the adezbelimab combined with trametinib regimen showed good safety in pediatric refractory relapsed LCH, with good drug tolerance. Both children benefited clinically from the combination regimen, preliminarily validating the feasibility and effectiveness of this regimen in treating refractory relapsed LCH in children. To systematically validate the clinical efficacy and safety of this combination regimen in treating refractory relapsed LCH, expand the sample size, and improve evidence-based medical evidence, this study plans to conduct a prospective single-arm, multicenter Phase II clinical trial of adebrelimab combined with trametinib for refractory Langerhans cell histiocytosis, aiming to optimize treatment regimens for children with refractory relapsed LCH and further improve clinical survival rates and long-term quality of life.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University
primary_outcomes: the quantitative Disease Activity Score, DAS
title: A Single-Arm,Multicenter Phase, Phase II Clinical Trial of Adebrelimab Combined With Trametinib in the Treatment of Refractory Recurrent Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis in Children and Adolescents

brief_summary:
This study aims to compare the chewing efficiency of implant-supported full-arch prostheses fabricated using two different jaw relation registration techniques: conventional static jaw relation registration and dynamic jaw tracking.

Ten completely edentulous patients will be recruited from the Department of Removable Prosthodontics, Faculty of Dentistry, Mansoura University. Each participant will receive implant-supported full-arch prosthetic rehabilitation according to the All-on-6 concept. Two definitive zirconia prostheses will be fabricated for each participant, one using conventional static jaw relation records and the other using dynamic jaw tracking records, in a crossover study design.

Chewing efficiency will be evaluated using a two-color chewing gum mixing test at the time of definitive prosthesis insertion, three months after insertion, and six months after insertion. The degree of color mixing will be analyzed using dedicated image-analysis software.

The study will investigate whether dynamic jaw relation registration provides different chewing efficiency outcomes compared with the conventional static technique in patients rehabilitated with implant-supported full-arch prostheses.
conditions: Chewing Efficiency in Completely Edentulous Patients Rehabilitated With Implant-Supported Full-Arch Prostheses
primary_outcomes: Chewing Efficiency Assessed by Two-Color Chewing Gum Mixing Test
title: Dynamic vs. Static Jaw Relations in Implant-Supported Prostheses: Chewing Efficiency

brief_summary:
This prospective observational cohort study aims to investigate the relationship between intra-abdominal pressure (IAP), respiratory system mechanics, and successful liberation from invasive mechanical ventilation in adult patients admitted to the intensive care unit (ICU) following emergency major laparotomy.

Increased intra-abdominal pressure may impair respiratory mechanics by reducing chest wall compliance, increasing airway pressures, and limiting diaphragmatic movement. These physiological changes may contribute to prolonged mechanical ventilation and difficulties in ventilator liberation.

The study will enroll 100 adult patients who undergo non-traumatic emergency major laparotomy with primary fascial closure and require invasive mechanical ventilation upon postoperative ICU admission.

Intra-abdominal pressure will be measured using a standardized intravesical technique through an existing urinary catheter. Serial measurements will be performed during the first 48 hours after ICU admission, alongside simultaneous assessments of respiratory system mechanics, including static respiratory system compliance and driving pressure.

The primary objectives are to evaluate the longitudinal association between IAP and static respiratory system compliance and to investigate whether early IAP trajectories are associated with time to successful liberation from invasive mechanical ventilation within 28 days.

Secondary outcomes include driving pressure, mechanical ventilation status on day 7, extubation failure, ventilator-free days through day 28, and mortality.

All clinical management decisions, including ventilator settings, sedation, spontaneous breathing trials, extubation, and tracheostomy, will remain under the responsibility of the treating ICU team. No study-directed therapeutic interventions will be performed.
interventions: Serial Intra-Abdominal Pressure and Respiratory Mechanics Assessment
lead_sponsor: Bursa Yuksek Ihtisas Training and Research Hospital
primary_outcomes: Association Between Intra-Abdominal Pressure and Static Respiratory System Compliance
Time to Successful Liberation From Invasive Mechanical Ventilation
title: Intra-Abdominal Pressure, Respiratory Mechanics, and Ventilator Liberation After Emergency Major Laparotomy

brief_summary:
The nursing education curriculum comprises both theoretical and practical courses designed to educate and prepare nursing students for their professional roles, functions, and responsibilities. Simulation, in particular, offers nursing students the opportunity to practice various essential clinical skills and decision-making processes in a safe environment, without posing an immediate risk to patients. Simulation-based training has been reported to be effective in teaching about pressure injuries. While the significance, staging, and care and treatment approaches regarding pressure injuries are addressed theoretically within nursing curricula, it is not always possible to provide all students with the opportunity to observe and experience pressure injuries at various stages in clinical practice settings. Therefore, teaching the stages of pressure injuries and the associated care and treatment processes through simulation applications in a laboratory setting is considered a significant educational strategy.

This study aims to determine the impact of low-fidelity simulation training on nursing students' knowledge levels regarding pressure injuries and their satisfaction with the learning experience.
title: The Effect Of Low-Fidelity Simulation Education Pressure Injuries

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether adding individualized pelvic floor muscle rehabilitation to standard urotherapy and alarm treatment improves bedwetting in children aged 5-18 years with primary monosymptomatic nocturnal enuresis.

Participants will be randomly assigned to two groups. Both groups will receive standard urotherapy and alarm treatment. One group will also receive pelvic floor muscle rehabilitation for 12 weeks. The study will compare dry nights, alarm activations, and changes in pelvic floor muscle function between the groups.
interventions: Standard urotherapy, Alarm therapy, Individualized pelvic floor muscle rehabilitation
title: Effectiveness of Individualized Pelvic Floor Muscle Rehabilitation in Addition to Standard Urotherapy and Alarm Therapy in Children With Primary Monosymptomatic Nocturnal Enuresis

brief_summary:
Hamstring tightness may be accompanied by limitations in flexibility and movement along the back of the body. Neuroathletic training combines exercises involving vision, eye movements, balance-related sensory input, and movement coordination. Its immediate effects on muscle activity and mobility require investigation.

This randomized study compared a single 20-minute neuroathletic training session with a 20-minute active control session in 40 adults aged 18 to 35 years with hamstring tightness. Participants were assigned to two groups of 20, with equal numbers of male and female participants in each group.

The neuroathletic training session included visual preparation exercises, eye movement drills, vestibular stimulation, trunk extension preparation, and visually guided movement tasks. The active control session consisted of light walking followed by non-ballistic dynamic stretching of the lower limbs, upper limbs, and trunk. Both sessions were supervised.

Before and after the assigned session, muscle activity was assessed in four muscle groups along the posterior chain using surface electromyography during the Superman exercise. Hamstring flexibility was assessed using an active knee extension test, and ankle dorsiflexion was assessed using a weight-bearing lunge test.

The study evaluated whether the immediate changes in these measures differed between neuroathletic training and the active control session.
primary_outcomes: Biceps Femoris Long Head Muscle Activation
title: Immediate Effects of Neuroathletic Training on Muscle Activity, Flexibility, and Ankle Mobility

brief_summary:
Surgical removal of impacted lower wisdom teeth can cause pain, facial swelling, difficulty opening the mouth, and discomfort during wound healing. This study evaluates whether placing a gel containing 0.2% hyaluronic acid into the tooth socket immediately after removal improves recovery compared with standard care alone.

Adults requiring removal of similarly impacted lower wisdom teeth on both sides of the mouth undergo two separate operations at least 28 days apart. Each participant receives hyaluronic acid gel in one socket, while the other socket receives no additional material. Both sockets are closed with stitches. The order of surgery and the side receiving the gel are randomly assigned. Participants are not told which side receives the gel.

Recovery is compared between the two sides of each participant. Pain and perceived swelling are recorded on days 1, 3, and 7 after each operation. Facial measurements and mouth opening are assessed before surgery and on days 3 and 7. Gum healing is assessed on days 3 and 7, and any complications are recorded. Participants receive the same routine postoperative care after both operations.
lead_sponsor: University of Medicine and Pharmacy at Ho Chi Minh City
title: Hyaluronic Acid Gel After Impacted Mandibular Third Molar Surgery

brief_summary:
This study will test whether six weeks of ashwagandha (KSM-66 root extract), helps teenage footballers recover and improve strength. Very little research has looked at young people aged 11 to 19, despite increased usage in this cohort.

About 50 to 60 male and female players from grassroots clubs in Sussex, Surrey and Greater London will be randomly assigned to take a daily capsule of either 450 mg ashwagandha or a placebo in an unblinded fashion. Before and after the six weeks, players will do tests at their usual training site: saliva samples to measure the cortisol, grip strength, a 1 km time trial, and short questionnaires on recovery, sleep, stress and soreness.

The results will show whether ashwagandha changes stress, strength, performance and perceived recovery over six weeks.
lead_sponsor: Sports Performance and Applied Research in Trials and Analysis
title: Effects of Root Extract Ashwagandha (KSM-66) on Perception of Recovery and Muscle Strength in Adolescents Aged 11 to 19 Engaged in Grassroots Football

brief_summary: In dry eye (DE), either insufficient aqueous tears are produced or the tears evaporate off the ocular surface too quickly. Meibomian gland dysfunction (MGD) results in poor quality or insufficient meibum being expressed during blinking, leading to a thinner tear lipid layer and faster aqueous tear evaporation. MGD is a major factor in evaporative dry eye globally. Activation of TRPM8 receptors on the cornea and eyelid margins gives a cooling sensation, which may increase the basal production of both aqueous tears and meibum through parasympathetic neural circuitry. The investigators hypothesize that acoltremon (TRYPTYR) 0.003% eye drops can increase tear lipid layer thickness and reduce the tear thinning rate.
title: Cooling Eyedrops for Dry Eye

brief_summary: This prospective cohort study aims to evaluate neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio, monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio, and neutrophil-to-monocyte ratio in children with lobar pneumonia, bronchiolitis, and bronchopneumonia compared with healthy children.
title: Neutrophil Monocyte Lymphocyte Ratios in Pediatric Chest Infections

brief_summary: This retrospective study evaluates whether providing clinicians with artificial intelligence (AI)-based kidney function results from a breath ammonia test can improve the quality of medication recommendations made by clinical pharmacists. Using historical inpatient cases from Shanghai Pudong Hospital, each case was evaluated under two information conditions: one with standard clinical information only, and one with the additional AI-based breath test kidney function results. Independent experts blindly scored the medication recommendations. The study aims to determine whether the breath test AI information adds meaningful clinical value to pharmacist decision-making.
primary_outcomes: Decision Score Difference Between Information Conditions
title: Impact of AI-Based Breath Ammonia Kidney Function Results on Clinical Pharmacist Medication Recommendations

brief_summary:
This project involves conducting integrated PET/MR or PET/CT imaging using a CAIX-targeted PET tracer (e.g., \[68Ga\]Ga-DOTA-CAIX peptide) in clinically diagnosed malignant tumor patients, aiming to achieve the following objectives:

Patients with malignant tumors: To visually assess the hypoxic state of malignant tumors, with pathological immunohistochemical detection of CAIX expression levels as the gold standard, evaluate the detection efficacy and quantitative accuracy of CAIX PET imaging for tumor hypoxic regions; clarify the location, extent, and heterogeneous distribution characteristics of hypoxic subregions within tumors; conduct a head-to-head comparison with \[18F\]FDG PET imaging to assess the complementary value and differences of the two imaging techniques in tumor boundary delineation, metastatic lesion detection, and tumor burden evaluation; based on the hypoxic biological information provided by CAIX PET imaging, assist clinicians in designing hypoxia-conformal margin expansion for radiotherapy target volumes, aiding in the determination of personalized radiotherapy and combined treatment plans.
interventions: Specific PET Imaging Agent Targeting CAIX
lead_sponsor: Union Hospital, Tongji Medical College, Huazhong University of Science and Technology
primary_outcomes: Visual and standardized uptake values assessment of lesions and biodistribution
title: The Clinical Application Value of CAIX-Targeted PET Hypoxia Imaging in Malignant Tumors

brief_summary:
This study looked at whether frontline healthcare workers could use a drug-free nasal spray twice a day for 8 weeks, whether it was safe, and whether they found it acceptable.

The spray used in the study (Profi Nasal Spray, Akita Biosciences) was a cosmetic nasal hygiene product made from ingredients already used in nasal and topical products.

Healthcare workers at a public hospital in New York City were randomly assigned to use the spray twice a day for 8 weeks or to receive no spray. The study asked:

* Feasibility: Could busy healthcare workers use the spray as directed over 8 weeks?
* Safety: Were side effects more common in people who used the spray than in people who did not?
* Acceptability: How did users feel about the spray, and did they stay in the study?

Every 3 days, participants answered a short online questionnaire about spray use, side effects, respiratory symptoms, and contact with patients who had COVID-19, influenza, or RSV. Spray use was checked by weighing the bottles at weeks 4 and 8.

To better understand acceptability, about 20 spray users also took part in one-on-one interviews about what it was like to use the spray, including ease of use, fitting it into a daily routine, and anything that made it harder to use.
primary_outcomes: Feasibility of using the nasal spray
Safety: Number of Participants With Adverse Events
Acceptability: Adherence to Daily Use and Study Dropout
title: Feasibility, Acceptability, and Safety of a Drug-Free Nasal Spray in Frontline Healthcare Workers

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of simulation-based training on medical waste management knowledge, attitudes, and practices among palliative care caregivers. This single-blind, two-center randomized controlled trial aims to determine the effectiveness of simulation-based training in improving caregivers' knowledge, attitudes, and practices regarding medical waste management compared to a control group.
primary_outcomes: Medical Waste Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Scale
title: Simulation-Based Medical Waste Training for Palliative Caregivers

brief_summary:
This study will test the safety and effectiveness of a drug called IM-1340 in participants with solid tumors. Participants will have solid tumor cancer that has spread through the body (metastatic) or cannot be removed with surgery (unresectable).

This study will have two parts. Part A will test increasing doses of IM-1340 to find out the safe dose and schedule of IM-1340 for participants. Part B will use the dose and schedule found in Part A to further study the safety of IM-1340 and if it works to treat solid tumor cancers.
primary_outcomes: Evaluate the safety and tolerability of IM-1340 in participants with advanced solid tumors
title: A Phase 1 Study of IM-1340 in Participants With Advanced Cancer

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effect of an integrated yoga and core stability exercises program on the severity of premenstrual syndrome symptoms and quality of life among nursing students.
conditions: Premenstrual Syndrome Symptoms and Quality of Life
primary_outcomes: Reduction in premenstrual syndrome symptoms severity
title: Integrated Core Stability Exercises and Yoga Program on Premenstrual Syndrome
