brief_summary:
This is a randomized, controlled, hybrid clinical trial evaluating the effects of the Evolv GLP-1 supplement on weight loss, blood sugar regulation, and appetite suppression over 12 weeks. Participants are randomized to either the intervention group (8 capsules daily) or a control group receiving standardized healthy eating guidance from the American Diabetes Association.

The study enrolls 98 male and female participants aged 18 and older with a BMI of 25-29.9 kg/m2. Primary endpoints include Hemoglobin A1c (HgbA1c) measured via bloodwork at Baseline, Week 6, and Week 12, as well as body weight and waist circumference measurements collected at Baseline, Week 4, Week 6, Week 8, and Week 12. Secondary endpoints capture participant perceptions of appetite suppression, weight loss, blood sugar, and overall well-being via self-reported questionnaires at the same time points.
title: A Controlled Study to Evaluate the Effects of a Supplement on Weight Loss, Blood Sugar, and Appetite Suppression

brief_summary:
This prospective, single-center, single-arm exploratory study will evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a pulsed field ablation system and a single-use pulsed field ablation catheter for the treatment of malignant lung tumors. Pulsed field ablation uses short electrical pulses to ablate targeted tumor tissue.

The study plans to enroll 15 adult participants at Shanghai Chest Hospital. Each participant will undergo bronchoscopic pulsed field ablation and will be followed for 6 months after the procedure. The main outcome is the proportion of treated lesions showing complete ablation at 6 months. Technical success, tumor control, survival, quality of life, and adverse events will also be evaluated.
interventions: Pulsed Field Ablation System and Single-Use Pulsed Field Ablation Catheter
title: Pulsed Field Ablation for the Treatment of Malignant Lung Tumors

brief_summary:
Partial nephrectomy is an operation that removes a kidney tumor while leaving the rest of the kidney in place. It is used to treat selected patients with small tumors confined to the kidney. Robot-assisted surgery allows the surgeon to control surgical instruments precisely during this procedure.

During standard surgery, the surgeon temporarily clamps the artery supplying the kidney to reduce bleeding while removing the tumor. The surgeon then closes the wound with stitches to help prevent bleeding and urine leakage. However, temporarily stopping blood flow and stitching the surrounding kidney tissue may affect how well the kidney works after surgery.

An alternative approach, called "off-clamp, sutureless" surgery, removes the tumor without clamping the kidney artery and uses materials that help stop bleeding instead of stitches to close the wound. This approach may reduce injury to healthy kidney tissue. Early studies, including research at the investigators' hospital, suggest that it may help preserve kidney function. However, stronger evidence is needed to determine how its benefits and risks compare with standard surgery.

This study will randomly assign participants to receive either off-clamp, sutureless robot-assisted partial nephrectomy or standard robot-assisted partial nephrectomy with artery clamping and stitches. The study will compare kidney function and surgical safety between the two groups. It will also examine whether the results differ according to how complex the kidney tumor is.

The findings may help identify which patients are most likely to benefit from the off-clamp, sutureless approach and guide the development of a standardized surgical procedure.
interventions: Conventional Robot-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy With Artery Clamping and Sutured Reconstruction
primary_outcomes: Decline in Estimated Glomerular Filtration Rate (eGFR) From Baseline to 3 Months After Surgery
title: Effect of Non-Clamping and Sutureless Technique on Postoperative Renal Function in Robot-Assisted Partial Nephrectomy

brief_summary: This study is a phase I, randomized, double-blind, placebo and active comparator-controlled clinical trial to evaluate the safety and immunogenicity of a trivalent split influenza virus vaccine (MDCK cell) developed by Sinovac Biotech Co., Ltd., in participants aged 6 months and above.
interventions: Cell-based Trivalent Split Influenza Virus Vaccine (cTIV)
Egg-based Trivalent Split Influenza Virus Vaccine (eTIV)
title: Phase I Clinical Trial of Trivalent Inactivated Split Influenza Virus Vaccine (MDCK Cell)

brief_summary: The study will evaluate the efficacy and safety of enicepatide, a glucagon-like peptide-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor (GLP-1/GIP) receptor agonist (RA), compared with tirzepatide among participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and inadequate glycemic control on oral glucose-lowering medications.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline to Week 72 in Glycosylated Hemoglobin (HbA1c, %)
title: A Clinical Study to Evaluate the Effects of Enicepatide Versus Tirzepatide in Participants With Type 2 Diabetes and Inadequate Blood Sugar Control on Oral Glucose-Lowering Medications

brief_summary:
This study will compare two different training methods used to improve sprint performance and hamstring strength in elite youth soccer players. Participants aged 16-17 years will be assigned to one of three groups: a sprint training group, an eccentric hamstring strength training group, or a control group. The two training programs will be performed for 6 weeks alongside the players' regular soccer and strength-conditioning training.

The main purpose of the study is to determine whether sprint training or eccentric hamstring strength training is more effective for improving sprint speed and sprint mechanical performance. Sprint performance will be assessed over 5, 10, 20, and 30 meters, together with mechanical variables derived from sprint force-velocity profiling. Eccentric hamstring strength will also be measured before and after the intervention.

The study will address whether a 6-week sprint training program can improve sprint performance and hamstring strength to a similar or greater extent than a targeted eccentric hamstring strength program. It is expected that sprint training will produce greater improvements in sprint-related performance, while eccentric hamstring training will produce greater improvements in eccentric hamstring strength.
title: Effects of Sprint and Eccentric Hamstring Training in Elite Youth Soccer Players

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to find out whether Caring Massage®, a Serenity room, or a combination of the two can improve organizational well-being among healthcare professionals.

The main question it aims to answer is:

Do healthcare professionals who receive one of these interventions report greater organizational well-being after 15 days than those who continue their usual post-shift routine? Researchers will compare each of the three intervention groups with a control group that receives no additional intervention. They will also assess whether any changes are maintained at the end of the intervention and 30 days later.

Participants will:

Be assigned to Caring Massage®, the Serenity room, an alternating combination of both, or the control group.

If assigned to an intervention group, attend two sessions per week for one month.

Complete questionnaires before the intervention, after 15 and 30 days, and 30 days after the intervention ends.
interventions: Combined Serenity Room and Caring Massage
primary_outcomes: Change in organizational well-being measured by the Short-Form Nursing Organizational Well-Being Questionnaire (QISO)
title: Holistic Approaches for Organizational Well-being of Healthcare Professionals

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to evaluate participant treatment experience with Povetacicept injection administered via autoinjector relative to Sibeprenlimab injection administered via prefilled syringe (PFS), and to assess the safety and tolerability of Povetacicept in participants with Immunoglobulin A nephropathy (IgAN).
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in the Self-Injection Administration Questionnaire (SIAQ) Scores at Week 12 After Transitioning to Povetacicept Injection
title: A Phase 3b Study of Participant Experience on Povetacicept Administered Via Autoinjector as Compared to Sibeprenlimab Administered Via Prefilled Syringe

brief_summary: Radiation dermatitis is a common and potentially treatment-limiting toxicity of radiotherapy for head and neck cancers. Colonization with Staphylococcus aureus has been identified as a risk factor for clinically significant radiation dermatitis, and bacterial decolonization has been shown to reduce moist desquamation in irradiated breast cancer patients. This randomized phase III trial evaluates whether a bacterial decolonization strategy can reduce the incidence of grade 2 radiation dermatitis with moist desquamation in patients receiving curative-intent radiotherapy (≥66 Gy) for cancers of the upper aerodigestive tract.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients with at least one grade ≥2 radiation dermatitis event with moist desquamation occurring during radiotherapy and up to 15 days following radiotherapy completion.
title: Bacterial Decolonization to Prevent Severe Radiation Dermatitis in Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate whether the addition of canagliflozin to levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (LNG-IUS) treatment, as compared with matching placebo or with the addition of metformin, increases the rate of pathological complete response (CR) at Week 24 in patients who wish to preserve fertility and who are overweight or have impaired glucose tolerance, type 2 diabetes mellitus, or polycystic ovary syndrome, with a diagnosis of atypical endometrial hyperplasia (AEH) or early-stage endometrioid endometrial carcinoma. The safety of this regimen and its effects on body weight, metabolic parameters, fertility, and long-term disease outcomes will also be assessed.
primary_outcomes: Complete remission (CR) rate of endometrial lesions at 24 weeks
title: Canagliflozin Plus Progestin for Atypical Endometrial Hyperplasia and Early-Stage Endometrial Cancer

brief_summary:
1. Burden:

   Women in Bangladesh face a high mental health burden, with 22% experiencing mental disorders compared to 16% of men. Access to face to face psychological care is limited by stigma, financial barriers, restricted mobility, and shortage of trained professionals, resulting in a major treatment gap.
2. Knowledge gap:

   Evidence on tele mental health effectiveness mainly comes from high income countries. In Bangladesh, evidence is limited to observational studies, and it remains unclear whether tele counselling is as effective as in person care for women.
3. Relevance:

This randomized non-inferiority trial will evaluate whether tele counselling can achieve comparable outcomes to face to face care. Findings will support policy decisions and scale up of accessible mental health services for women in Bangladesh, aligned national, global and institutional goals.

Hypothesis (if any):

1\. Tele based counselling through WBC is hypothesised to be non-inferior to in person counselling in improving women's mental health outcomes, quality of life, and overall wellbeing, with comparable acceptability, accessibility, and usefulness.

Objectives:

This study aims to evaluate whether tele based counselling through Wellbeing Centres is a clinically non-inferior and feasible alternative to in person counselling for improving women's mental health and quality of life in Bangladesh.

Methods:

The investigators propose a two-arm randomized controlled non-inferiority trial among 1200 women with moderate to severe depression or anxiety. Participants will be randomized to tele counselling through Wellbeing Centres or standard face to face counselling using identical protocols. Outcomes including PHQ-9, GAD-7, WHOQOL-BREF, WHO-5, and GHQ-12 will be assessed at baseline and 2, 4, and 6 months. Quantitative and qualitative analyses will evaluate clinical effectiveness, feasibility, acceptability, accessibility, usability and treatment experiences.

Outcome measures/variables:

Primary outcomes are changes in depression (PHQ-9) and anxiety (GAD-7) scores. Secondary outcomes include quality of life (WHOQOL-BREF), psychological distress (GHQ-12), mhGAP conditions, wellbeing (WHO-5), and service acceptability, accessibility, and usefulness. All measures will be assessed at baseline and at 2, 4, and 6 months.
lead_sponsor: International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh
title: Improving Women's Mental Health Through Tele-based Wellbeing Centres in Bangladesh.

brief_summary:
The goal of this quality improvement protocol is to compare the evaluations between video laryngoscopes (VLs) available in the University of Colorado Health Hospital at Metro Denver operating rooms (ORs).

With the feedback from survey answers collected, they will be translated into quantifiable data to easily review the VL usability and efficiency per VL device.
title: OR Video-Laryngoscope Evaluations

brief_summary:
Objective: This prospective, single-center, observational clinical study aims to evaluate changes in qCON (hypnotic depth), qNOX (nociception/analgesia depth), EMG, and other parameters in patients undergoing elective cesarean section under general anesthesia, with a focus on the induction and maintenance phases.

Background: Primary goals in cesarean anesthesia include maintaining adequate anesthetic depth to prevent awareness and intraoperative recall, preserving uterine tone, and avoiding neonatal respiratory depression. While high inhalation agent concentrations increase uterine relaxation and bleeding risks, opioids administered during the incision-to-delivery interval can cause neonatal respiratory depression. Alternative anesthetic combinations (e.g., ketamine-propofol) are used in practice, but their effects on EEG-derived indices (qCON and qNOX) and potential paradoxical shifts remain poorly defined.

Methods: The study will be conducted at Erciyes University Faculty of Medicine Hospital in 140 patients planned for elective cesarean section under general anesthesia (alpha = 0.05, 90% power, effect size = 0.50), including a history of eclampsia, preoperative sedative use, and difficult intubation.
primary_outcomes: Evaluation of Consciousness Depth (qCON) changes during induction
Evaluation of Analgesia Depth (qNOX) changes during induction
Evaluation of electromyography (EMG) changes during induction
Evaluation of standard hemodynamics (HR, MAP, SpO2, EtCO2) changes during induction
title: Evaluation of Consciousness Depth (qCON) and Analgesia Depth (qNOX) Indices in General Anesthesia

brief_summary: This study is a single-center, open-label, controlled study. Its primary objective is to evaluate the 20-year persistence of immunity induced by the inactivated hepatitis A vaccine. At least 106 healthy participants aged 21-28 years will be enrolled. Participants will be selected from individuals who completed the full vaccination course in the PRO-HA-4006 clinical study (Three-Batch Consistency Study of Healive® in Healthy Children Aged 1-8 Years in Changzhou) . After voluntarily providing informed consent, each participant will undergo one venous blood collection of approximately 3.0 mL for hepatitis A antibody testing to assess the persistence of immunity induced by the hepatitis A vaccine.
primary_outcomes: Seropositivity rate and geometric mean concentration (GMC) of hepatitis A antibodies at Year 20 after vaccination.
title: Study on the Long-Term Persistence of Immunity Induced by Inactivated Hepatitis A Vaccine

brief_summary: Educational interventions play an extensive role in the literature on hypertension disease management. It has been reported that patient education practices increase individuals' level of knowledge, improve sleep and quality of life, ensure the control of hypertension, are effective in developing self-management skills, reduce body weight and body mass index, are effective in controlling harmful lifestyle habits, increase treatment adherence and healthy lifestyle behaviors, improve health literacy and self-efficacy levels, positively affect rational medication use, and strengthen adaptation to the disease. Accordingly, educational interventions for patients with hypertension play a fundamental role in improving treatment success and long-term health outcomes by supporting individuals' active participation in disease management. However, most studies conducted in the context of hypertension have focused on medication adherence, blood pressure control, or the physiological effects of lifestyle changes. In contrast, no study examining the effects of educational interventions for disease management on the health perception and burnout levels of individuals with hypertension has been found in the literature. The aim of this study is to determine the effects of disease management education provided to individuals diagnosed with hypertension on their health perception and burnout levels. The study aims to provide practical implications for both individual patient outcomes (psychosocial variables) and healthcare practices (the planning and implementation of patient education programs).
primary_outcomes: health perception will be measured using health perception scale.
title: THE EFFECT OF EDUCATION IN PATIENTS WITH HYPERTENSION

brief_summary:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study will evaluate the effect of intravenous dexamethasone on postoperative analgesia in children and adolescents undergoing surgery for idiopathic scoliosis with bilateral erector spinae plane (ESP) blocks.

Participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to receive intravenous placebo, dexamethasone 0.1 mg/kg, or dexamethasone 0.2 mg/kg. All participants will receive standardized general anesthesia, bilateral ultrasound-guided ESP blocks, and multimodal postoperative analgesia.

The study will evaluate postoperative opioid requirements and the duration and quality of postoperative analgesia. Secondary outcomes will include postoperative pain intensity, time to first rescue opioid administration, the proportion of participants requiring rescue opioid analgesia, postoperative nausea and vomiting, blood glucose concentrations, and adverse events.

The study aims to determine whether intravenous dexamethasone improves postoperative analgesia following ESP block and whether the analgesic effect differs between the two studied dexamethasone doses.
title: Intravenous Dexamethasone for ESP Block Analgesia in Children Undergoing Idiopathic Scoliosis Surgery

brief_summary:
This clinical trial will test individual wellness coaching for 44 nurses who provide cancer care. Wellness means balance across physical, emotional, social, and other areas of life.

The main questions are:

Does wellness coaching improve nurses' quality of life at work?

Does wellness coaching improve nurses' wellness?

Nurses will be grouped according to their work area: inpatient wards, intensive care units, or outpatient clinics. Within each work area, researchers will assign nurses by chance to one of two groups. Each nurse will have an equal chance of joining either group.

One group will receive individual wellness coaching for eight weeks. The control group will continue usual work routines without receiving wellness coaching or educational materials from the research team during the assessment period. An informational brochure about wellness coaching will be offered after completion of all scheduled outcome assessments, including the assessment three months after the intervention period. Researchers will compare changes in quality of life and wellness between the groups.

Participants will:

Attend individual coaching sessions in person if assigned to the coaching group. Sessions will take place once a week for eight weeks. Each session will last about 45 to 50 minutes.

Answer questionnaires before the intervention period and immediately after it.

Answer questionnaires again one and three months after the intervention period.

Coaching will focus on exploring personal needs and setting goals. Topics will include strategies for looking after their health, managing stress, and balancing work and personal life.
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Professional Quality of Life: Compassion Satisfaction Subscale Score
Change From Baseline in Professional Quality of Life: Burnout Subscale Score
Change From Baseline in Professional Quality of Life: Compassion Fatigue/Secondary Traumatic Stress Subscale Score
Change From Baseline in Wellness Wheel Total Score
title: Effects of Wellness Coaching on Quality of Life and Wellness in Oncology Nurses

brief_summary:
The study was designed with a parallel-group randomized controlled experimental design to determine the effects of podcast-based education on climate change awareness and climate change health literacy levels of nursing students. A podcast-based climate change awareness education will be implemented as the study's intervention. Participants in both groups will complete a pre-test. The experimental group will then receive four sessions of podcast-based climate change awareness education, while the control group will receive no intervention during this phase. After the four sessions, both groups will complete a post-test simultaneously. Subsequently, participants in the control group will receive the same four-session podcast-based educational intervention. Following completion of these sessions, both groups will complete a follow-up assessment at the same time.
